Iran and Ceasefire U.S. and Iran conclude first round of direct talks in Switzerland: Delegations from the United States and Iran met in the mountain resort town of Burgenstock, Switzerland, on Sunday for a single day of high-level negotiations towards a final U.S.-Iran deal that should be reached within 60 days, according to the MOU signed by both parties, with technical talks set to continue for the rest of the week. The U.S. delegation for the meeting included Vice President Vance, Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and top advisors to Vance and Witkoff. Iran's delegation included Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, senior SNSC official Ali Bagheri, Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati, National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard, and other senior political, economic, and diplomatic officials, according to Iranian state media. The delegation called itself the "Minab 168," in reference to a U.S.-Israeli airstrike on a girls' school in the southeastern city in February, which killed up to 168 people, most of them children. Pakistani and Qatari mediators were also present. The talks primarily focused on Israel's continued attacks on Lebanon, which the first clause of the memorandum of understanding requires it to cease, and came after Iran said it would close the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday in protest of continued Israeli attacks on Lebanon. At the talks, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi briefly in the same room with VP Vance, but departed when cameras were present, rejecting what they called an American "media show." Previous to the talks, U.S. Vice President JD Vance securing a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah would be one of the two main priorities at talks in Switzerland, alongside discussions about the Iranian nuclear file. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei had said that his delegation's trip was strictly about "demanding that the other side fulfill its obligations," noting that the first clause of the U.S.-Iran MOU requires hostilities to stop on all fronts, including Lebanon. He the United States has "either been unable or unwilling" to enforce that provision, and Israel has continued to violate the agreement. Pakistan-Qatar statement highlights key outcomes from Sunday negotiations: According to a statement put out by mediators from Pakistan and Qatar, the United States and Iran adopted a 60-day roadmap toward a final agreement and agreed to immediately begin further technical negotiations. Other key outcomes included: A High Level Committee was established to oversee implementation of the memorandum, with chief negotiators leading working groups on nuclear issues, sanctions, and dispute resolution. The parties agreed to establish a Lebanon deconfliction cell, facilitated by Pakistan and Qatar and involving Lebanon, to help enforce provisions aimed at ending military operations in Lebanon. Washington and Tehran also created a direct communication channel to prevent misunderstandings during implementation and help ensure the safe passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. Vance says "great progress" made in Iran talks: Vance said the latest U.S.-Iran talks made "a lot of good progress" and laid "a very good foundation" for a final agreement, describing the negotiations as "very good." Vance said that while the Iranian delegation had threatened to walk out over threats issued by Trump regarding their reported closure of Hormuz, talks continued past 1 a.m., adding: "They didn't walk out, and their technical team is still here in Burgenstock working with our technical team." He claimed that International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors are expected to return to Iran to verify compliance with a preliminary agreement. On frozen Iranian assets, Vance said Washington wants to ensure any released funds "go to help the people of Iran and not to fund terrorism," outlining a proposal involving Qatari oversight and the purchase of "American corn and American wheat for the benefit of the Iranian people." The Iranian response: Iran's Araghchi described the Lebanon mechanism as the agreement's "first real test," while saying the mediation had already helped secure progress on "the lifting of the blockade," waivers for Iranian oil and petrochemical exports, the release of some frozen assets, and the launch of a major reconstruction and development plan for Iran. Report says Israel debating "limited withdrawals" from parts of southern Lebanon: Israel is considering "limited withdrawals" from parts of southern Lebanon, including areas within the buffer zone, a report from Israel's Channel 12 citing senior Israeli officials said Sunday. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday that Israel would maintain a presence in the "security zone" of southern Lebanon "for as long as necessary." "Nothing will alter that commitment." After Iran announced the closure of the Strait over Israeli attacks in Lebanon on Saturday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz reportedly the Israeli army to cease fire without withdrawing from their positions, according to Al Jazeera's Zeina Khodr. More below. Iran announces Strait of Hormuz closure on Saturday: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Saturday that, "in light of the United States' clear bad faith and failure to implement the first clause of the war-ending memorandum of understanding" and "in response to the continuous ceasefire violations by the Zionist regime in southern Lebanon," the Strait of Hormuz would be closed to traffic effective immediately. It threatened "further measures had been planned and will be implemented" if Israel's aggression continued. On Sunday, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright that 67 ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, following Friday's total of 55 ships, claiming that "in terms of oil and oil products," the present situation is "about equal" to the period before the conflict. Windward, a maritime tracking firm, only 12 transits on Sunday, and 32 transits on Saturday, however. Iran reportedly Hezbollah that it would not reopen the Strait until Israel announced publicly that it would comply with the "comprehensive" ceasefire in Lebanon and end its military operations there. Trump threatens Iran, addresses ceasefire in Fox News interview: As his delegation met with their Iranian counterparts in Switzerland on Sunday, President Donald Trump Iran in a Truth Social post, saying that it must "stop [its] highly paid PROXIES in Lebanon from causing trouble." "If they don't," he warned, "we'll hit Iran very hard again, just like we did last week, only harder!!!" Also on Sunday, he Fox News that he would "take over the rest of the country" of Iran, warning that Iran "won't have a country "if it continues to close the Strait of Hormuz. In the same interview, he threatened to kill the Iranian officials on a diplomatic mission to Switzerland, saying that they would not "make it back" to Iran if the Strait remained closed. Trump's threats Clause 1 of the memorandum of understanding, which commits both sides to "refrain from the threat or use of force against each other." Trump described the current memorandum of understanding as a ceasefire extension rather than a final deal, saying he still has a "60-day option" and can "do whatever I want" afterward if Iran fails to meet U.S. demands. Pezeshkian says uranium enrichment not on the table: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday that Tehran would not give up its right to enrich uranium, and announced the upcoming return of $6 billion in frozen Iranian assets from Qatar. "What the United States demands is that Iran not build an atomic bomb. This is nothing new, and we can also state in writing that we have no intention of building a bomb," Pezeshkian added. "However," he added, "we will not relinquish our right to enrichment, and the other side will have no choice but to accept this right." Pezeshkian also announced that "with the negotiation process beginning today, our $6 billion blocked in Qatar will return," referring to Iranian oil revenues frozen by the U.S. Lebanon Killed and wounded: At least 4,106 people have been killed and 12,153 wounded in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since March 2, according to the Lebanese Health Ministry. Israel continued its assault on southern Lebanon through Saturday despite "ceasefire": On Friday, the same day as the announcement of a "ceasefire" deal, Israeli strikes killed at least 83 people and wounded 141 others in southern Lebanon. Israel its overnight air and drone strikes across the Nabatieh and Jezzine districts into Saturday. At least 70 Israeli airstrikes between midnight and 3 p.m. on Saturday killed 38 people across 22 villages, according to Lebanon's L'Orient Today. One of the deadliest attacks--on the village of Qanaarit--killed 10 people, mostly women and children. Qanaarit, in the Saida district, is sheltering people displaced from villages farther south. Israeli attacks four members of two different families in Sohmor and Arabsalim. In Barish, an Israeli strike killed an entire family, including two children. After 3 p.m. on Saturday, southern Lebanon went 19 hours without any reported Israeli airstrikes, artillery shelling, or other major violations, the longest period of relative calm in 110 days, according to L'Orient Today. On Sunday evening, Israeli drones two locations, one on the outskirts of Farah in Nabatieh al-Fawqa and the other, a roundabout in Kfar Tibnit. The strikes occurred as the Lebanese Army's commander in chief was visiting Nabatieh. No Israeli attacks have been reported so far on Monday. Hezbollah kills at least six Israeli soldiers: Hezbollah at least six Israeli soldiers and wounded more than 20 during Israel's campaign in Lebanon over the weekend, according to Israeli military reports. Hezbollah accuses Israel of "never accepting" the terms of a ceasefire: In a statement Saturday, Hezbollah Israel had "never accepted" the ceasefire terms, accusing it of trying to justify continued attacks through false allegations against the group. Hezbollah said it remains committed to the ceasefire but "will not tolerate" attempts to seize additional territory or expand Israel's occupation in southern Lebanon. On Sunday, Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem Israel's continued military presence in southern Lebanon is "impossible," and warned that Hezbollah will respond to any Israeli violations. He also the hypocrisy surrounding the ceasefire. "A ceasefire means Hezbollah does not fire and Israel is free to occupy anywhere!" he said. "We do not want such a ceasefire." Qassem added on Sunday that Hezbollah enjoys the "great support" of Iran, and praised the country for backing and working diligently to implement a ceasefire in Lebanon. On negotiations, Qassem said that the Israeli regime had given Lebanon "nothing" in the past few months, and said that it had only employed "deception" in its direct talks with the Lebanese state. He advised the government not to yield to those demands, saying that doing so would only impair its sovereignty. Katz insists no Israeli troop withdrawal from southern Lebanon: Israeli defense minister Israel Katz insisted on Sunday that Israeli troops would not withdraw from Beaufort castle--also known as Qalaat al-Shaqif--in southern Lebanon. "Israel has no intention of withdrawing from the Beaufort, which is an integral part of the security zone in Lebanon and essential for the defense of the Galilee settlements and IDF forces," Katz . "As prime minister Netanyahu and I have clarified - Israel will not withdraw from the security zone in Lebanon." Israel kills Lebanese environmental activist Mona Khalil: Lebanese environmental activist and world-famous turtle conservationist to her injuries on Friday after an Israeli strike hit her home two weeks ago. The strike also wounded her Ethiopian housekeeper. Khalil trained a generation of volunteers in turtle conservation, working on the Mediterranean coastline where endangered sea turtles travel to lay their eggs. "They knew exactly who Mona Khalil was," wrote journalist Marwa Osman about the Israeli strike that ultimately killed Khalil. "They knew the bright orange house in Mansouri, south Lebanon. ... It was one of the most recognizable symbols of environmental conservation on Lebanon's southern coast; a sanctuary dedicated to protecting endangered sea turtles and preserving life." Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, three Palestinians were killed and 11 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. At least 17 Palestinians were killed by Israel in Gaza over the weekend. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,035 killed, with 173,368 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,024 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,260, while 784 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli strikes kill medic and student in Gaza: A Palestinian medic was after an Israeli airstrike hit a civilian vehicle in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis on Monday, according to WAFA. In a separate attack, a female student, on her way to sit for her secondary school examinations, was killed and several others wounded when Israel a vehicle in the Al-Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City. Four Palestinians killed on Sunday: Israeli drone strikes killed at least four Palestinians, including a child, and wounded others across Gaza on Sunday, as Israel continued breaching the ceasefire. Two Israeli attacks hit Khan Younis, and one hit Al-Shati refugee camp in Gaza City. Drop Site contributor Mohammed Ahmed filmed from Al-Shati. A resident of the camp described to Ahmed a strike on a tent that killed one. "There is nowhere safe," he told Ahmed. He said he rarely leaves his tent, and when he does, even for a 100-meter walk, "I entrust myself to God," fearing any car or person nearby could be the next target. Ahmed's video dispatches from the scene are and . Israeli attacks kill 10 in Gaza on Saturday: Israeli airstrikes and gunfire at least 10 Palestinians across Gaza on Saturday, including two young girls. In the Bureij camp in central Gaza, an Israeli strike on a group of people killed three. In Gaza City, a pre-dawn strike on an apartment killed four people, including two young girls and a woman. A 9-year-old boy was critically wounded in the attack and had his leg amputated. An Israeli attack near Khan Younis killed one and wounded 8 others. Another strike and gunfire killed a woman in Beit Lahiya and a man near the Saftawi junction in Northern Gaza. Israel kills Palestinian journalist in Gaza: Israeli forces Palestinian journalist and cameraman Ahmad Samir Washah during an attack on the Al-Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza on Saturday. Washah worked for Al Jazeera Mubasher. His brother, journalist Mohammed Samir Washah, was assassinated in an Israeli drone strike on his car on April 8. Israel killed both brothers in a span of 73 days. Ahmad's sister her brothers at Washah's funeral on Sunday in footage provided by Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah. Ahmad "wanted to be with Mohammed, and Mohammed wanted Ahmad," she said. "Their souls are intertwined." "He was a lion, and more," she added, describing him as a "thorn" in Israel's side, reflecting on his fearless journalism. Desalination plants in Gaza are shutting down because of Israeli fuel restrictions: Israeli restrictions on fuel entering the Gaza Strip some desalination plants to cease operations on Friday and Saturday, according to Gaza's Association of Desalination Plant Owners. The sector, which provides much of the Strip's drinking water, is "significantly suffering" from a "severe shortage of operational and maintenance supplies," they wrote--a product of Israeli policies. Only 14.8% of the quantity of fuel agreed upon in the October ceasefire agreement has been allowed into Gaza, according to Palestinian reports shared with mediators and obtained by Drop Site. Israeli forces kill two Palestinians, demolish homes and conduct mass arrests across West Bank: Israeli forces attacks across the occupied West Bank on Monday. In Beit Ummar, north of Hebron, two teenage boys, 15 and 19 years old, were killed by Israeli forces and settlers, according to WAFA, which said the pair were left bleeding before their bodies were withheld. Two other young men were wounded by Israeli gunfire in the town. A 50-year-old woman was also assaulted and injured during an Israeli raid on the village of Kafr Qalil near Nablus. In Jerusalem and Bethlehem, Israeli forces demolished two multi-story buildings and two homes, while also detaining dozens of Palestinians during raids across multiple areas. At least 70 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces and settlers in the occupied West Bank since the start of 2026. U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Major week for primaries: New York, Maryland, and Utah will hold critical primaries. In New York, Israel has become a fissure in three high-profile races, with Claire Valdez (NY07), Darializa Avila Chevalier(NY13), and Brad Lander (NY10) running as a Zohran Mamdani -backed slate. Just north of the city, Israel critic Effie Phillips-Staley is running in NY17 for the nomination to take on Mike Lawler , arguably the most outspoken defender of Israel in Congress. In another Manhattan race (NY12), Alex Bores is running to rein in artificial intelligence, a test of the AI industry's power, which has spent millions to stop him. Valdez and Avila Chevalier will appear on Breaking Points later Monday. or Site contributor Michael Lange to stay abreast of the New York races. In New York's 13th district, a former energy minister from the Dominican Republic an incendiary, racist attack against Chevalier, accusing her backer, Mamdani, of attempting to replace Dominican political power with Haitian voters. Both Darializa and her opponent, the incumbent Adriano Espaillat , are Dominican. Boafo faces last-minute scramble to stop him: The Washington Post on Sunday finally covered the AIPAC-dominated congressional race in the paper's backyard of southern Maryland, highlighting the $11 million AIPAC and crypto have put behind him. Adrian Boafo was a top aide to outgoing Rep. Steny Hoyer , a leading AIPAC ally who organized the bi-annual congressional delegation to Israel. He is also a federal lobbyist for Oracle, founded by Larry Ellison , the largest donor to Friends of the IDF and the new owner of TikTok and, through his son David Ellison , CBS News, and much of the rest of the media. The most viable candidate to be able to stop Boafo, according to sources in the district with access to internal polling, appears to be Quincy Bareebe , a progressive health care business owner who has self-funded her campaign. In Utah, the populist-progressive field is split between Liban Mohamed and Nate Blouin , which may make space for center right former Rep. Ben McAdams to sneak through. U.S. military kills two in boat strike in Caribbean: The U.S. military conducted a boat strike in the Caribbean on Sunday, killing two people. SOUTHCOM posted a of the strike and said, "Two male narco-terrorists were killed during this action, and there were six male survivors." The U.S. has killed more than 200 people in over 60 strikes on vessels in the Pacific and Caribbean since September. FEC filings reveal Republican-linked PAC funded super PACs in Democratic primaries : New FEC filings two pop-up super PACs, Real Change PAC and Lead Left were entirely funded by Conservative Americans PAC, a Republican-linked group. The super PACs spent more than $4.3 million across Democratic congressional primaries in Texas, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Nebraska, and Maine. The groups helped elect Maine state auditor Matt Dunlap and advancing Denise Powell in Nebraska, but failed to defeat winning candidates, including Pennsylvania's Bob Brooks. The group also spent over $1 million to boost Maureen Galindo in Texas, a candidate who was castigated by her party for her antisemitic remarks. Galindo was defeated by her opponent, sheriff's deputy Johnny Garcia. Trump appointees halted investigation into clemency for fraud convict, officials say: Trump's political appointees an early-stage investigation into whether improper payments helped secure a clemency grant for David Gentile , a private equity executive convicted in a $1.6 billion fraud scheme, according to The New York Times. Federal prosecutors in Brooklyn were examining whether Gentile offered $2.5 million to facilitate his release, including to the Rev. Frank Mann , a retired priest and friend of Trump's. Mann denied involvement and the inquiry was abandoned in May. Jim Jordan-linked super PAC receives dark money from private prison company: The American Liberty Foundation, a super PAC tied to Rep. Jim Jordan , $250,000 in "dark money" payments last year from GEO Group , a private prison company that runs ICE detention centers, according to a report by Pogo Investigates. Trump on Capitol Hill: President Trump is set to join the Senate GOP lunch on Wednesday. The discussion among Republican senators is expected to center on the SAVE America Act, a bill significantly restricting access to voting rights that Trump has incessantly advocated for ahead of upcoming elections. Senate Majority Leader John Thune has indicated the legislation does not have enough votes to pass the Senate, hence his reluctance to bring it to the floor for a vote, with several GOP senators, most notably Sen. Thom Tillis , Sen. Lisa Murkowski , and Sen. Susan Collins expressing opposition. Democratic senator allegedly misused campaign funds: Ruben Gallego , who has been about the nature of his longtime friendship with disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell , spent campaign dollars on tickets to the Super Bowl in 2023 via a joint account with Swalwell, according to a report in Politico. He also spent money on family vacations to Miami, Disney World and Disneyland, as well as babysitting expenses paid directly to his mother-in-law. Minnesota Senate candidates debate: The first debate between Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan and Congresswoman Angie Craig centered on campaign finance reform and immigration policy. Flanagan criticized Craig's campaign funding from large super PACs and special interest groups, as well as her vote to pass the Laken Riley Act, which unconstitutionally mandates ICE and CBP detention of undocumented immigrants strictly based on prior, unproven arrests. Craig focused her messaging on fraud in Minnesota, claiming that Flanagan and the Walz administration failed to enforce existing laws. While Craig has a significant advantage in dollars raised, Flanagan has consistently led in the polls and won the endorsement of the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party. Van Hollen discusses presidential run: Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen a potential presidential run on the "On NOTUS" podcast earlier this week, saying he was "kicking the tires a bit" following visits to early primary states. Van Hollen that senior Biden administration officials responsible for U.S. policy on Gaza should not serve in a future Democratic administration unless they acknowledge they were wrong, saying that Washington has a culture of "no accountability." Other International News British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces resignation: Starmer on Monday he is stepping down as leader of the Labour Party and will remain in office until a new Labour leader is chosen by the party. It will be the UK's seventh prime minister in 10 years. Starmer led Labour to a landslide election victory in July 2024, but since then his popularity has plummeted and he is widely seen as having betrayed the left wing of the party. Former Manchester mayor and newly elected Labour MP Andy Burnham is widely expected to become the next Prime Minister. Read Paul Holden 's . Initial count shows far-right presidential candidate de la Espriella leading in Colombia: Millionaire and self-proclaimed "outsider" Abelardo de Espriella leading the quick count in Colombia's presidential runoff on Sunday, against left-wing senator Ivan Cepeda. De La Espriella's lead amounts to 250,830 more votes than Cepeda out of nearly 13 million votes cast. Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Espriella and President Trump said he had won "BIG" in a post on Truth Social. The news was also celebrated by Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, Venezuelan opposition figure Corina Machado, and Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro. During his campaign, Espriella threatened to "disembowel" the left, pledged to build "mega-prisons," and threatened to kill criminals like "rats and cockroaches." Petro that there were irregularities in the preliminary vote count. He accused Israel of interfering in the elections, citing changes to the national registry's server IP addresses. He called for a full audit and recount. Cepeda called for patience as the official count advanced, saying he would challenge the results at voting centers that presented alleged irregularities. Explosion reported in Qatar: An "internal explosion" at Qatar's Ras Laffan gas facilities 58 people and left 18 others missing on Sunday, authorities said. The explosion was precipitated by "a technical incident, according to Qatar's interior ministry. Two roadside bombs kill at least seven in northwest Pakistan: Two roadside bombs at least seven people and injured three in Bannu district near the Afghan border on Saturday, the Associated Press reported. There was no immediate claim of responsibility, and President Asif Ali Zardari condemned the attack, warning against support for "internal and external handlers of terrorism." RSF drone strike on Kosti fuel station kills one, injures 14: A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on a fuel station in Kosti, White Nile State, one civilian and injured 14 others on Sunday, Sudan Tribune reported. The RSF has recently intensified attacks on energy infrastructure in White Nile and its neighboring North Kordofan state, destroying several fuel stations and causing severe fuel shortages. Separately, the Sudanese army intensive drone strikes on Saturday, targeting RSF positions and movements across North Kordofan state to foil preparations for an assault on the state capital, El Obeid, military sources told Sudan Tribune. The strikes hit areas including Um Samima, Abu Gaoud, and Hamrat al-Sheikh. Bolivia declares state of emergency to clear protest blockades: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz a 90-day state of emergency on Saturday, empowering the military to remove road blockades that have isolated La Paz and disrupted fuel and food supplies amid weeks of protests against his austerity measures. At least 17 people have died in the unrest and 365 have been arrested. The protests, led by highland Indigenous and rural workers' groups, erupted over Paz's elimination of fuel subsidies. Rural workers' federations that they would continue to strike in the country, journalist Ollie Vargas reported. At least 15 migrants found dead off Libya 's eastern coast: The bodies of at least 15 migrants ashore near Tobruk over the past week after their boat, carrying around 61 people, was believed to have capsized, Reuters reported on Saturday. Officials said more bodies could still be found. Separately, medics in Khumas treated 13 migrants after another boat capsized off Libya's coast, a route that has drawn migrants fleeing conflict and poverty since the 2011 fall of Muammar Gaddafi. China places U.S. defense companies on export control list: China added 10 U.S.-based companies to its export control list and barred government procurement from 46 U.S. firms as part of an escalating trade war with Washington. The move comes about two weeks after the Pentagon expanded its list of companies it says are linked to China's military and are banned from contracting ties, including major firms such as Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD. The newly blacklisted U.S. companies include U.S. defense contractors involved in drones, radar, shipbuilding and aerospace. Ukrainian drone war targeting Moscow escalates: Russia said it shot down over 300 drones overnight, including 84 that targeted Moscow and briefly halted flights at airports near the capital. The drone raids came after Ukraine claimed a high-profile strike on a satellite communications center near Moscow, as well as the destruction of Moscow's only oil refinery last week. Russian drone and missile attacks also struck multiple Ukrainian regions, killing at least six people, including a 13-year-old boy, his father, and his grandmother in Sumy, two people in Zaporizhzhia, and one person in Odesa, after an Iskander missile hit an agricultural facility. body:
One of the ugliest voices in the New Hampshire State House, Rep. Travis Corcoran (R), took a swing at me because I told my story of being the kid of immigrants, helped deport a war criminal, but am fighting against the horrors of Trump’s ICE goons.
Who is Rep. Corcoran? He is a notorious merchant of hate. He had his guns taken away after he endorsed the shooting of Congresswoman Gabby Gifford in 2011, he proudly calls for white people to use the n-word, throws around homophobic slurs, and recently called for a jewish lawmaker to face the “final solution.” And when I got death threats by the far right, he cheered that on.
He can come at me all he wants.
I can take it.
I’m not going anywhere.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
The person I had deported was the far-right murderer of Victor Jara.
Victor Jara, was a beloved folk singer murdered by the fascist Pinochet regime. For Chileans he is what Bruce Springsteen is to Americans.
Because of his reputation as an advocate for poor Chileans and for social justice, when the Pinochet government took control in a violent coup in 1973, Jara was abducted, tortured in front of a packed soccer stadium, executed, and his body was publicly displayed as an example.
In the mid 2000s Victor Jara’s wife hired my law firm pro-bono to bring his murderer to justice. As one of the firm's only Spanish speaking lawyers I spent a year traveling to Chile tracking down leads and conducting interviews.
Ultimately we uncovered the identity of his killer and hunted him down to the US where he had become a citizen and assumed a quiet new life (built on lies) running a pizzeria outside of Orlando, Florida.
When you become a US citizen one of the questions that you must answer is have you ever tortured anyone. In court, we were able to prove he had lied about this in his naturalization process, in turn we were able to have him stripped of his citizenship and deported back to Chile to face justice for war crimes. Now he is facing justice in Chile, and should spend the rest of his life in a Chilean jail cell.
So to respond to Travis: I am proud of what I did, war criminals should absolutely be held to account and if they came here under false pretenses, they should be deported. Hardworking immigrants like my parents and the millions presently targeted by ICE (which should be dismantled) should be left to pursue the American dream.
My background and the threat I pose to MAGA (I am poised to ensure open seat NH-01 stays blue) have put a massive target on my back — the NRCC has been attacking me since day one, Nazis stormed a rally of mine, and last month leaders of New Hampshire’s far-right called for my public hanging.
We’re rolling with the punches but we need your support to keep fighting. Please can you rush a donation of $25, $10, or even just $5 to ensure a progressive fighter takes this critical seat? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
DONATE TODAY!>> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-nh1]
Thank you in advance for your support at this inflection point for our campaign.
Christian Urrutia
Democrat for NH-01

Peter,
Last week, I was in Brussels, Belgium, and Strasbourg, France, as a part of the Sustainable Energy & Environment Coalition’s (SEEC) House Delegation to meet with European Parliament and Council members and business leaders in the renewable energy sectors across Europe.
As a mom, a lung doctor, a critical care physician, and now a member of Congress, I’ve seen firsthand what happens when we ignore threats to our health and our future. Climate change isn't a distant problem. It's already affecting the air we breathe, the communities we call home, and the natural places we cherish.
We can't turn back the clock and pretend the dangers posed by fossil fuel pollution don't exist. Wildfires, extreme heat, poor air quality, and increasingly severe weather events are putting families at risk every single day.
That's why I'm fighting for investments in clean energy, environmental protection, and a healthier future for the next generation. The choices we make now will determine the world our children inherit.
I'm committed to making meaningful climate progress, but I can't do it alone.

[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
If there’s
one thing you should understand about my campaign, it’s this:

I am fighting for a Michigan where everyone — from our kids to our seniors
— can stay and thrive.

I’ll tell you more about what I mean in a second, but first: [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/6862?t=1001&akid=1692%2E181023%2EpwrcFe ]Michigan
is one of the most competitive states in the country, and our opponents
have the backing of big billionaires and special interests. I can only win
this race with your support — so can I count on you to chip in?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/6862?t=1002&akid=1692%2E181023%2EpwrcFe ]Donate →

I was
raised in a middle class household where we believed in the values of hard
work, opportunity, and serving others.

I carried those values with me throughout my entire career — and because
of that, I’m proud to say that I’ve been able to make a significant impact
on the barriers facing hardworking Michiganders.

From defending people’s civil rights and freedoms in a courtroom in
Detroit, to expanding scholarships and freezing tuition at Wayne State Law
School, to today, where I’ve fought to expand voter access as Secretary of
State, I’ve held true to the same core belief: Michigan should be a place
where everyone gets a chance to succeed.

But this work is far from finished. Across our country, we’re seeing
widespread attacks on our most vulnerable populations, policies that make
life harder for working families, and politicians that would rather spout
talking points than actually deliver real results.

That’s not the kind of future I want for our state — and that’s why I’m
running for governor.

I’m
running to make sure that Michigan will always be a place where the
government pushes people forward instead of holding them back. And as
governor, my promise to you is that I’ll use every tool available to make
life easier — so that every Michigander has a chance to thrive in our
beautiful state.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/6863?t=1003&akid=1692%2E181023%2EpwrcFe ]That’s the kind of future I’m hoping to build, and if anything I said
resonates with you, I’d be honored if you pitched in today to help me win
this competitive race →

subject: Happy Pride Month
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1529%2E1086043%2ENnKF5Z)
Peter, Happy Pride Month.
Nobody should have to justify their own humanity. As long as I am Governor of Maryland, we will fight for the humanity, rights, and freedoms of every single person in our state – including our LGBTQ+ community. **_That's a promise we intend to keep._**
While Washington works to strip away rights and demonize families, Maryland is — and will remain — a safe haven for the LGBTQ+ community. We've signed the Trans Health Equity Act. We launched the first-in-the-nation program to reduce suicides among LGBTQ+ youth. We've fought for HIV prevention and care across our state.
**And we cannot and will not stop fighting.**
But that fight has a cost. MAGA Republicans and Trump's allies are coming for everything we've built, including the progress we've made for LGBTQ+ Marylanders.

I'm grateful for this team. – Wes Moore

subject: My father’s legacy and lesson

Friends,
Yesterday I shared some reflections on my dad [https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1HHj7C1Zis/] on social media to mark Father’s Day. The responses have meant so much to me and to my mother that I wanted to share the post with this list as well.
Blessings, Tom
FATHER’S DAY POST
Without fail, someone stops me on the campaign every day to share a story – and often a hug and a few tears – about how my father, Dr. Vito Perriello, touched their lives.
Campaigns extract a lot from a candidate, so I want y’all to know that these stories are a huge source of restoration for my soul. I want to say thank you, and also to offer a reflection on two ways that these stories land differently with me now than when I last ran for Congress in 2010.
The first difference is just time and healing. Dad passed so suddenly in 2009, and the loss was so raw in 2010, that each story shared was somehow both a salve and salt in a still gaping wound. Now, with 16 years somehow passed, I get to experience those same stories as almost pure joy, knowing that his legacy pulses through the lives of generations that are still alive and honoring his memory.
The second difference is that, with a bit less hair and a bit more wisdom, I finally feel like my dad’s true superpower has been revealed. I had assumed it was his great pediatric power to heal, and that legacy was my sister Paige’s to inherit.
But the passage of time has allowed me to discern a more profound throughline in the stories you share – my father’s magical ability to make invisible people feel seen, to make marginalized people know that they mattered. He and his partners built Pediatric Associates to provide not only the highest quality of care to kids, but also to apply it equally to every kid, regardless of race or class.
That’s the major key in which these stories always harmonize, particularly from African American and rural elders: “Your daddy – he really listened to me.” “Dr. P, he took so much time with us.” “When my daughter was struggling, I cannot tell you how many doctors and hospitals just dismissed us. Until we met your dad.”
He had the white coat and credentials after his name, yet still honored each parent’s concern for their child as he would want someone to respect his concern for me or my siblings.
Maybe it was his humble roots. Maybe it was his faith. What I know for sure is that he made every child and every parent feel like they mattered, because they really did matter to him.
And that superpower was the true inheritance he offered to all of us. It’s what I aspire to have at the heart of my life and my campaign. His values are the armor we need to fight back against those trying to make cruelty and caste systems seem cool.
I count myself blessed every day for every day I got with my father. And I am grateful for the lessons he continues to reveal to me these many years later through the stories you’ve shared.

A federal judge just gave him a simple opportunity: submit a signed declaration confirming that Donald Trump's "Anti-Weaponization Fund" is dead and won't move forward.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
How JD Vance found his way back to faith | | | |
---
| | | Fellow Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: How JD Vance found his way back to faith | | | | | | | Fellow Patriot, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Fellow Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

# [Fed "Maestro" and Wall Street Northstar Alan Greenspan dies at 100](https://substack.com/redirect/9b3cff28-5ee3-49b5-b795-c9e0e59991ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Alan Greenspan, the influential Federal Reserve chairman known as the Maestro who served nearly two decades and warned of irrational exuberance in 1996,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a5f1b745-bea9-4139-9a61-2e85af221f34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[died Monday at home from Parkinson's complications,](https://substack.com/redirect/a5f1b745-bea9-4139-9a61-2e85af221f34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** his wife Andrea Mitchell announced.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b3cff28-5ee3-49b5-b795-c9e0e59991ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Longest Serving Leader:** Greenspan chaired the Fed from 1987 to 2006 under four presidents, guiding through Black Monday, recessions, 9/11 attacks and dot-com shifts while fighting inflation.
* **Famous Market Signal:** His televised remark on asset values being unduly escalated briefly sank Tokyo stocks three percent and rattled others though markets recovered until the 2001 bust.
* **Purposeful Obfuscation:** The economist deliberately used convoluted language in testimony to sidestep direct answers while still shaping policy and calming markets as a titan of capitalism.
* **Diverse Early Roots:** Born in 1926 to a stockbroker father, he played jazz saxophone in bands, studied economics with Ayn Rand influence and earned his doctorate at age 51 after advisory roles.

# [Microsoft's AI power hunger to be fed by Chevron and 20 years of Texas natural gas ](https://substack.com/redirect/9b3cff28-5ee3-49b5-b795-c9e0e59991ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b3cff28-5ee3-49b5-b795-c9e0e59991ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Massive Power Setup:** Majority electricity will come from large gas turbines by GE Vernova and Caterpillar located directly at the data center site in Reeves County.
* **Investment Decision Looming:** Project has not begun construction yet though Chevron expects final go-ahead later this year for reliable power delivery.
* **AI Growth Driver:** Microsoft plans $190 billion dollars capital expenditures this year, a 61% increase, seeking scalable energy beyond renewables for constant artificial intelligence needs.
* **Permian Supply Edge:** Chevron will deliver competitively priced natural gas quickly from the west Texas basin to match 24/7 data center demands as stated by its new energies president.

| Mass GOP Demands Governor Healey End Her Silence on Rampant Benefits Fraud and Fully Cooperate with Federal Investigators
BOSTON, MA - The Massachusetts Republican Party today called on Democrat Governor Maura Healey to immediately stop ignoring the explosion of government benefits fraud in the Commonwealth and to direct her administration to fully cooperate with the U.S. Attorney's Office.
"This level of fraud is completely out of control, and Governor Healey's continued silence is unacceptable," said Amy Carnevale, Chairwoman of the Massachusetts Republican Party.
Federal authorities announced Thursday the arrest and charging of 15 individuals accused of stealing $1.4 million in SNAP, MassHealth, disability, and unemployment benefits. This latest action is part of an ongoing crackdown that has already charged more than 60 defendants in connection with $63 million in alleged fraud since December. Yet despite this alarming scale of abuse, Governor Healey's administration has refused to provide critical state benefits data to federal prosecutors, even suing in court to block access to records paid for by federal taxpayers.
She continued, "Hardworking Massachusetts families are footing the bill for tens of millions of dollars stolen through identity theft, fake IDs, and illegal schemes while the Governor refuses to lift a finger to help stop it. Enough is enough. She must end her obstructionism and immediately provide full access to state data so federal investigators can root out every instance of waste, fraud, and abuse."
U.S. Attorney Leah Foley and Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald have publicly highlighted the governor's office refusal to assist, noting that state cooperation would streamline investigations and uncover far more wrongdoing.
Instead, Massachusetts data remains under a protective order, forcing federal authorities to rely on slower, less effective methods while fraud continues unchecked.
The MassGOP demands that Governor Healey immediately:
* Direct all relevant state agencies to provide full, unrestricted access to benefits data for federal fraud investigations.
* Cease all legal efforts to block federal access to taxpayer-funded records.
* Publicly commit to working with the U.S. Attorney's Office to protect Massachusetts taxpayers from further abuse.

"Every dollar stolen through these schemes is taken directly from the paychecks of Massachusetts workers and families," Carnevale continued. "Governor Healey's refusal to cooperate is a betrayal of the public trust. Taxpayers deserve transparency and accountability, not stonewalling and excuses. The Massachusetts Republican Party will continue fighting for full cooperation and aggressive action until every instance of fraud is exposed and stopped."
The Massachusetts Republican Party urges all residents concerned about government waste and fraud to demand action from Governor Healey and their elected representatives.

subject: Early Voting for August 4th GOP Primary is Underway

body:
Join me, Doug Ollivant. Cast your vote early for the August 4th Primary.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/dN0yZBFHj3z?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

**Dear Fellow Patriots in Virginia’s 7th District,**
[**Early in-person voting for the August 4th Republican Primary is underway.**](https://us.list-manage.com/eISn6L5Wn4H?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)**** This is our moment to nominate a fighter who will put America First, stand strong for our God-given freedoms, and defeat Eugene Vindman in November.
[**I’m Doug Ollivant.**](https://us.list-manage.com/2WsDwVHEwJT?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)**** A rock-solid conservative who will always defend your constitutional rights, especially the Second Amendment. Without the right to bear arms, we cannot protect the First Amendment or fight tyranny. I will never let the progressive left erode the freedoms that make America exceptional.
I am ready on Day 1 to serve VA-7. My lifetime of service from leading troops in combat, advising commanders on the battlefield, at the White House National Security Council, and consulting in the boardroom, has prepared me for decisive action with no learning curve and no swamp delays.
I am not a career politician. I’ve been running hard to be your candidate since the beginning - living and breathing the 7th District every day because this is my home.
This is OUR home. I didn’t run away like Yevgeny Vindman did when he wanted an easier race. I didn’t pick this district because I thought it would be convenient or waited to see which way the wind was blowing.I’m a devoted father of seven, husband, grandfather of two, combat veteran, and your neighbor in Culpeper County. [**I understand our communities, from family farms to growing suburbs, because I live them with you.**](https://us.list-manage.com/vnBSdjOA10r?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
I’m the only Republican in this primary with the [**name recognition and appeal**](https://us.list-manage.com/185IOFmo9au?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0) to beat Vindman and take back Virginia’s 7th.
**Vote early in person or by mail** and make your voice heard. [**Check with your local registrar for hours and locations (many offer convenient weekend voting).**](https://us.list-manage.com/lLBRwmZvvra?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0) This primary is critical. Let’s nominate a proven patriot who will fight for secure borders, strong families, and economic freedom that will put America First.
Thank you for your support. Together, we will keep Virginia and America great! ****

**Candidate for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

### NEWSLETTER FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,
It has been another busy and rewarding few weeks serving our community. I am especially excited to share that **Governor DeSantis has signed HB 429 into law,** legislation inspired by conversations with Ocala Police Chief Mike Balken and his team. I also had the opportunity to celebrate our Marion County students,**** support our veterans, and continue promoting policies that help keep Florida strong.
As always, please do not hesitate to [**contact my office**](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=517c213c6e&e=d1c1b9864f) if there is something we can do for you. My team and I would be more than happy to help you in any way we can.
---
| |
### HB 429 Signed by Governor DeSantis!
---
|
---
| | **Governor DeSantis signed HB 429 into law,** and I couldn't be prouder of this one. This bill, **co-sponsored with Rep. Jessica Baker,** modernizes how Florida identifies and prosecutes criminal gang activity, giving law enforcement real tools to protect our communities.
**This legislation was born out of a conversation with Ocala Police Chief Balken and his team.** They flagged the gap; we fixed it. That's how it's supposed to work.
Thank you, Chief Balken and the Ocala PD, for bringing this forward, and Governor DeSantis for signing it into law. Florida families are safer because of it.
---
| |
### Veterans Helping Veterans
---
|
---
| | **I had the opportunity to tour Veterans Helping Veterans and see firsthand the incredible work they do to support those who have served our nation.**
From connecting veterans with resources and services to providing a strong sense of community, their dedication to improving the lives of fellow veterans is truly inspiring. Thank you to the staff, volunteers, and veterans who shared their stories and showed me the impact of this important organization.
---

Congratulations — your hard work paid off.

### 100% Pro-Business Voting Record

|

body:
This atmosphere of fear has NO place in Ohio politics

| | | | | | |
If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, you can unsubscribe [here](https://us.list-manage.com/xXLJNVbLPWF?e=b5ea5bcc17&c2id=a48c62b2ec1a8ba6dd0ee9d07b5fb11a).

Friend, this month, the FBI executed a massive, unprecedented raid on a nonpartisan voting rights organization in Ohio.

These agents didn’t just seize computers — they showed up at the _private homes_ of volunteers and staff members without warrants and used aggressive tactics.
**Let’s be entirely clear about what this is:** This is a coordinated attempt to intimidate everyday Ohioans and weaponize federal agencies to suppress voter registration.
And if we allow this to become the norm, it will only get worse as we march toward the 2028 presidential election.
_**This**_**is what happens when we have leaders who circulate lies without evidence about our election security. And, it’s why we need leaders in Columbus ready to hold the line for our constitutional rights.**
I’m not afraid of this administration’s intimidation tactics. This atmosphere of fear has NO place in Ohio politics, and if you agree, I need your help:
**Ohio is ground zero for Trump’s attacks on our voting rights. And right now, I’m up against a Republican who is taking a page straight out of the administration’s fear mongering strategy.**
[**If you believe Ohioans deserve leaders who will put our voters first and refuse to backslide on our hard won voting rights, please consider pitching in what you can to my campaign today:**](https://us.list-manage.com/gBDk2CbH9wE?e=b5ea5bcc17&c2id=a48c62b2ec1a8ba6dd0ee9d07b5fb11a)

I want to tell you something that’s not easy to talk about...
A sitting Republican elected official recently tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media and wrote: "I would like to report a foreign occupier. Name: Unpronounceable. Country of origin: Tatooine." He was talking about me. The same official called for the mass deportation of Indian Americans.
I was born in New Delhi. I came to this country as a baby. I grew up in Peoria, Illinois. I went to public schools, got on food stamps for a time with my family, worked my way to Princeton and Harvard Law. I served in government. I got elected to Congress four times.
And someone still looked at all of that and saw a foreign occupier.
I'm telling you this not for sympathy. I'm telling you this because what happened to me is happening to communities all across this country right now, at a scale we have never seen before.
Trump and his MAGA allies have made it clear: if you weren't born here, if your name is hard to pronounce, if you look different or pray differently, you are not fully American in their eyes. They are using the machinery of the federal government to make that point, loudly and cruelly, every single day.
My father came here with nothing. He believed this country would be there for families like ours. It was. Barely. Because people fought for it.
That is exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
We need leaders in office who will stand up for immigrant families and for every community that Trump has decided to make an enemy.
Those leaders exist. They are running for office right now. They need our support.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kelly for New Hampshire, Christopher Connelly Treasurer, PO Box 4723 Manchester, NH 03108
body:
Join us as we march with Governor Ayotte in the Amherst and Merrimack 4th of July parades.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/iRoPjEJ1u2f?e=38cb9f3df0&c2id=d600a7f798f5b28227ceda5411445d39)
| | | | | |
Friends,
As we celebrate Independence Day and kick off America’s 250th Birthday celebration, we hope you’ll join Governor Ayotte at the Amherst and Merrimack 4th of July parades.
The 4th of July is a time to celebrate the freedoms we cherish, honor those who have defended them, and reflect on the values that make America the greatest nation in the world. As we begin commemorating our nation’s 250th birthday, there is no better way to show our pride in our country and our state than marching together with fellow supporters.
We would love to have you join us as we show our support and celebrate this special day with communities across New Hampshire.
**Amherst 4th of July Parade** 📍 Wilkins Elementary School, 80 Boston Post Road, Amherst🕘 Lineup begins at 9:00 AM
**Merrimack 4th of July Parade** 📍 O’Gara Drive, Merrimack🕛 Lineup begins at 12:00 PM
Whether you can join us for one parade or both, we would be thrilled to have you march alongside Governor Ayotte.
If you would like to attend, please click [HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/twDixI3adzl?e=38cb9f3df0&c2id=d600a7f798f5b28227ceda5411445d39) to RSVP.
We look forward to celebrating Independence Day with you and continuing to keep New Hampshire safe, prosperous, and free.
With gratitude,
Team Kelly

name: =?utf-8?q?Mar=C3=ADa_Teresa_Kumar=2C_Voto_Latino?=
subject: Birthright citizenship shouldn’t be up for discussion
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
The human cost of reversing birthright citizenship is this:
#
We are standing on the edge of a precipice, Peter.
Any day now, the Supreme Court will hand down its decision in _Trump v. Barbara._
On its surface, the case evaluates the constitutionality of an executive order attempting to end birthright citizenship.
But let’s be entirely clear about what is actually on trial: the Supreme Court is deciding whether to uphold the text of our Constitution or whether to hand a sledgehammer to the executive branch to dismantle the very bedrock of the American promise.
[**Will you chip in right now to help Voto Latino protect that promise and scale up our defense and protect our community’s fundamental rights?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260622-1.MDOHH7&refcode=em20260622-284&t=1&akid=284%2E1366028%2EAOUnwR)
For over 150 years, the 14th Amendment has offered a baseline guarantee of equality — if you were born on American soil, you’re an American. Period. Now, that foundational right is being treated like a political bargaining chip.
This isn’t an isolated debate about constitutional semantics. It is a direct, calculated assault on the dignity, security, and rightful place of Latino families in our democracy.
The human cost of an adverse ruling is this:
\- **It targets our youth** — Latinos represent 75% of all children with noncitizen parents in the United States.

\- **It’ll tear families apart** — It threatens over 14 million people who are part of mixed-status families, introducing a devastating rupture into households where siblings could suddenly hold entirely different legal realities.

\- **It sparks a retroactive nightmare** — It puts approximately 1.8 million current U.S. citizens born to unauthorized parents, the vast majority of whom are Latino, at risk of having their citizenship stolen away.
The gatekeepers of the status quo look at the changing demographics of our nation and see a threat to their own grip on power. **Our community is entering its peak earning years, starting families, and stepping into our civic power. Every 30 seconds, another young, entrepreneurial Latino in this country turns 18 years old.**
And instead of adjusting their policies to meet a changing America, they choose a darker path.
Right now, we must make it clear that our position is unshakeable: birthright citizenship is not up for negotiation. _Our children are not collateral damage in a political power play._
They are trying to build an artificial dam against the demographic and democratic future of this nation. They are attempting to erase the Latino community from the American promise — but we know our history, we know our power, and we will not be erased.
**[Peter, will you rush an emergency donation of any amount today to help Voto Latino mobilize voters, defend our communities, and organize until our rightful place in this country is secured?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260622-1.MDOHH7&refcode=em20260622-284&t=2&akid=284%2E1366028%2EAOUnwR)**
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260622-1.a2B9Bi&amount=3&refcode=20260622-284&t=21&akid=284%2E1366028%2EAOUnwR)**
Thank you for reading,
Maria Teresa Kumar
Co-founder and CEO, Voto Latino

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-voto-footer?refcode=em20260622-284-&t=22&refcode2=284_1366028_AOUnwR&akid=284%2E1366028%2EAOUnwR)**

This is what a grassroots movement looks like...

| | | | | [|

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

**This is what a grassroots movement looks like...**
A few weeks ago, we were canvassing in the Nevada Heights neighborhood in Spokane. I knocked on the door of a young family with two kids. They were in a rush, of course, but they shared that the mom recently had to quit her job in order to take care of the kids full-time because childcare would be too unaffordable.
Stories like these are all too common; both in District 5 and throughout the country. Which is exactly why I am fighting for a**Universal Childcare** solution. Universal childcare would put thousands of dollars back in the pockets of Eastern Washington families every year.
This year, we have a unique opportunity to make the change happen to build a better future. We are building a movement that is people powered and unapologetically fights for the working class. No Corporate PACs, just grassroots. I am so proud to have people knocking on doors that _never_ have before.

The primary is just six weeks away, and we're doing this without any paid consultants. Every dollar you give goes directly to knocking on doors like that one in Nevada Heights, having face-to-face conversations with families across District 5.
Here's what your contribution puts to work between now and primary day:
* **$10** covers a yard sign that shows our movement is grounded in the people
* **$25** pays for snacks and drinks for our canvassers
* **$100** funds direct outreach to an entire precinct
* **$250** helps us fund our postcard campaign to engage as many voters as possible

If you would like to go above and beyond in supporting this movement, please consider hosting Kevin for a **house party or meet and greet**. Nothing beats meeting new people in person! Please reach out directly to info@kevinfaganforcongress.com if you are interested in hosting.

| | | | | | | | | | | | That mom in Nevada Heights shouldn't have to choose between her career and her kids. No family should. Whether it is Universal Childcare, Medicare for All, or Right to Repair, we are fighting for policies that _put people first_.
Six weeks. No corporate PACs. Just us.
Thank you for being in this with me.
Kevin
**P.S.** If you've already given, the most powerful thing you can do right now is forward this to one person. That's how grassroots wins.

# Robber Baron Exploits
---

For this week’s Robber Baron Exploits, let’s take a look at Chewy. Yes, Chewy, the online pet food and supply company that originated in Florida in 2011. In 2017, it was purchased by PetSmart. PetSmart is backed by a private equity firm BC Partners. BC Partners is a British company.
Chewy has gradually increased its services from an online pet food and supply company to a “tele-triage connect” with a vet program, a compounding pharmacy, pet insurance programs and wellness plans. More recently, Chewy has been busy with vet care, offering well visits, urgent care visits, and surgeries for pets. It was announced April 8, 2026 that Chewy has signed an agreement to acquire Modern Animal a “technology driven veterinary company with 29 clinics and100,000+ member clients.” With this merger, Chewy will expand its vet practice from 18 to 47 clinics. Chewy Health president, Mita Malhotra was quoted in the acquisition announcement saying, “The joining of Modern Animal’s best-in-class operating systems and clinical expertise with Chewy’s unparallelled customer acquisition and engagement engines creates an industry-leading, high [return on investment] business almost immediately.”
And there it is pet owners. Chewy, a pet supply company and wannabe vet that is owned by a British private equity firm wants to turn your pet’s vet care into a for profit business so private equity can get richer! How much profit will Chewy make off of your cat’s antibiotic prescription and rabies vaccine? Will you be able to afford to get your dog spayed or neutered? Local vet practices are small businesses with very thin margins. It’s incredibly difficult to get into vet school. It’s expensive to go to vet school. Vet students have to be smart, hardworking, and give much of their youth to studying to enter the veterinarian profession. Plus, the student loan programs in this country with their outrageous interest rates only adds to the burden of fulfilling their dream. If they make it through, they will become small business owners and fulfill their dream of caring for their communities’ large and small animals. As Chewy buys up the market, will they force your local vet practice to sell to them? Will this be another instance of Walmart killing your country store? Will this turn the noble veterinarian profession into hourly employees in a for-profit workplace where vets will be overworked and their employer will dictate the kind of vet care they can give?
Is this the start of private equity ruining yet another sector of our economy, both for those who dedicate their lives to their profession as well as the customers that need these services? Will anyone be able to afford pets in a few years at this rate? Why must private equity monetize every aspect of our lives? Private equity firms should be regulated to protect small businesses who profit from _serving_ their customers. We don’t need any more consolidation into large corporations that use their market clout to profit _at the expense of_ their customers. Pay attention and fight back against these exploitative robber barons
Yours,
**Rosemary Rox**
