subject: A reflection on Juneteenth.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Seligman for AG,
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2?refcode=x_260622_juneteenth_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_dhs_email-26q2?refcode=x_260622_juneteenth_act]
I’m hoping you took some time to reflect on the significance of Juneteenth over the weekend. As a campaign, we were able to celebrate with the community in Denver's historic Five Points neighborhood.
Juneteenth is a celebration of liberation—a day that marks the moment when freedom was finally recognized for thousands of enslaved people in Texas, years after the Emancipation Proclamation.
But it is also a reminder that the fight for true freedom, justice, and equality did not end there.
I’ve been reflecting on what it means to say we are fighting for the rule of law, especially when, for generations, the law has too often failed Black and Brown communities.
The truth is that our legal system has not always protected everyone equally. Our most vulnerable communities have been denied dignity, opportunity, and justice because of systems that were built to exclude them. We must do better.
That is the work ahead of us.
As attorney general, I will fight for a Colorado where justice is not something reserved for the powerful, but something every person can count on. I will use the law to protect all people, hold powerful interests accountable, and continue the work of building a fairer and more equal future.
Celebrating Juneteenth is essential. And now, we keep doing the work of building a better future for everyone.
Happy Juneteenth.
David

body:
By rejecting corporate cash, Brad is proving we can do politics differently.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41489%2E3422442%2ECpo8tE)
Peter,
**Tomorrow, we have the chance to send a leader in the fight against corporate money in politics through to the general election: Brad Lander.**
Brad is running for Congress in New York, and his primary election is tomorrow. **[Can you help him win by splitting a donation between his campaign and Truth to Power?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260622_1_ak.pYNnev&refcode=em20260622-41489&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41489%2E3422442%2ECpo8tE)**
Too many politicians rely on massive corporations and special interests to fund their campaigns, and then—unsurprisingly—fail to hold them accountable once elected. But like me, **Brad doesn’t take a single dime of corporate PAC money.**
By rejecting corporate cash, Brad is proving we can do politics differently. We know he’ll fight for us in Washington because his support comes from people all over the country chipping in what they can, when they can.
But the truth is, the corporate checks his opponent takes could make the difference in a race this competitive. The only way we beat their deep pockets is by stepping up for Brad right now.
**[Will you split $5 or more between Brad’s campaign and Truth to Power right away to give him the late resources he needs to win?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260622_1_ak.pYNnev&refcode=em20260622-41489&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41489%2E3422442%2ECpo8tE)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260622_1_ak.pYNnev&refcode=em20260622-41489&t=22&akid=41489%2E3422442%2ECpo8tE)
I’m proud to stand with Brad, and I hope you’ll join me before polls close tomorrow night.
Thank you,
Katie Porter

I want to be real with you for a minute:
What we're up against is no joke.
On the other side of this race sits an entrenched MAGA candidate with a Rolodex full of millionaire and billionaire backers, a network of dark money groups, and the full weight of the Republican establishment behind them.
They've done this before. They know how to leverage fear and political games to win. And they are not taking us lightly.
They watched us sweep every parish in round one, and they picked up the phone. They started making calls. Cutting checks. Building the kind of war chest that's supposed to make campaigns like ours fold up and go home.
That's how they keep power. They make the cost of challenging them so high that most people don't even try.
I'm not most people. I'm a farmer who's spent a lifetime doing hard things, and we’re starting to generate national attention on this race. But attention alone won’t get the job done.
We need resources to get our message to every corner of this state. To make sure voters know the runoff is happening and what's at stake. To counter the inevitable wave of MAGA attack ads that are already being planned.
I've talked to Republicans who are quietly rooting for us. Independents who've never voted Democrat who are reconsidering. Lifelong Louisianans who are done watching their state bleed jobs, farms, and dignity while career politicians in Washington serve their donors instead of their constituents.
That coalition can win. I've seen it with my own eyes on this campaign trail.
But it only comes together if we have the resources to reach those voters. And that's where you come in.
Every dollar you give right now is a direct counterweight to MAGA's millionaire backers. It's proof that this movement is real. That we're serious. That we're not going anywhere.

Just $5.
$5 because control of the House could come down to a handful of districts like this one.
$5 because national Republicans have made Southwest Washington one of their top targets, and they're prepared to spend whatever it takes to flip this seat.

name: Deb Haaland
subject: Being Fierce is a commitment to never back down
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
No one can Be Fierce alone.
Peter, it’s Deb Haaland and I am officially the Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico. **[Will you split a donation of $5 between Heartland Patriots and my campaign right now to help us hit our first $50,000 general election goal and start this race strong?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105502?refcode=em20260622-10591&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=5&t=1&akid=10591%2E614464%2EIwAgIF)**
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105502?refcode=em20260622-10591&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10591%2E614464%2EIwAgIF)**
Because of this grassroots team, we won — and Peter, that’s what it means to Be Fierce.
You may have noticed it throughout this campaign, how I sign my emails, what I say on TV, and how I talk with voters. I always come back to the same saying: Be Fierce.
Be Fierce in how we show up for our families. Be Fierce in how we fight for working people. Be Fierce when powerful interests try to tell us what’s possible and what isn’t.
It’s a reminder to push forward and break ceilings, like I did as one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and later as the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history — and because of what we’re doing together right now, when we win this race, I will be the first Native American woman elected Governor in any state.
Being Fierce is also a commitment to never back down. I learned that in Congress when I stopped Donald Trump from threatening our public lands and our communities, and again at the Department of the Interior when I rebuilt after cuts, rollbacks, and attacks on conservation and working families.
**And now, when healthcare is gutted, costs go up, and the affordability crisis is ignored, I won’t back down, I will Be Fierce. I will fight for working families across New Mexico and deliver real results, not excuses, and I will be sure to leave the ladder down for the next generation.**
But, Peter, no one can Be Fierce alone. This race is already one of the most competitive in the country. Billionaires and national Republicans are preparing to spend whatever it takes to flip New Mexico, and we can’t afford to start slow. **[Will you chip in $5 or anything you can to Heartland Patriots and my campaign right now to help power this movement to November and Be Fierce in this fight?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/105502?refcode=em20260622-10591&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=5&t=3&akid=10591%2E614464%2EIwAgIF)**

On June 10, 2026, Lee Raymond, the CEO of Exxon and then ExxonMobil from 1993 to 2005, passed away. Raymond was, without a doubt, a world-historic figure--a man who helped devise one of the most impactful conspiracies in all of human civilization. Those actions will be the core of his legacy, as demonstrated already by the headlines reporting his death in papers from the other side of the world ("[Exxon CEO Lee Raymond, the 'Darth Vader of global warming', dies at 87](https://substack.com/redirect/e19fd1ba-0c41-4c9c-b473-2b588c1be4af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)") to his home state of Texas ("[Lee Raymond, former Exxon CEO who denied climate change, dies at 87](https://substack.com/redirect/c44cf07a-b758-49d0-8bf5-3caedd34f44c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)").
That's because Raymond played a lead role in ExxonMobil's--and the entire oil and gas industry's--campaign of climate deception, which set us on course for the planetary crisis that is playing out today.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..RYMRqDILuiEXhSzmQ5qoGQZTC91f4m9WfeM4AfPGy5E?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=203113037)
This was a knowing conspiracy. Raymond and his colleagues running fossil fuel corporations understood decades ago that the unchecked burning of fossil fuels would, in the words of their own senior employees' internal communications, be "[globally catastrophic](https://substack.com/redirect/fbb8bbe0-fa9d-43b2-93c8-a5e66278fb04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," do "[great irreversible harm to our planet](https://substack.com/redirect/fbb8bbe0-fa9d-43b2-93c8-a5e66278fb04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," have "[serious consequences for man's comfort and survival,](https://substack.com/redirect/6d95344f-226a-4e74-a9e5-9ea64ba4443e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" and cause such destabilization that "[civilization could prove a fragile thing](https://substack.com/redirect/a0fd3075-c48d-4e48-aeee-9cce68e4cae4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)."
Upon learning about the world-historic harm they were causing, Raymond and his ilk could have opted for a less lethal business model. They could have alerted the public and regulators. At the very least, they could have remained silent and let the rest of us solve the civilization-threatening crisis they were creating.
They did none of these things. Instead, they spread climate denial to block the development of clean energy alternatives--or, in the words of a 1988 [Exxon strategy memo](https://substack.com/redirect/d49c2494-7404-4e5e-b59c-06b8d227f917?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), they "emphasize[d] the uncertainty of scientific conclusions" to resist the "development of nonfossil fuel resources"--so they could continue wringing profit from destroying humanity's only habitat for as long as possible. Indeed, they lied about climate science even as they [relied](https://substack.com/redirect/5d2baf6d-19f4-4444-950a-858ba1fdc2cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on it themselves to adapt their pipelines and offshore oil platforms to the extreme weather disasters they were causing. Truth for them; lies for everyone else.
To the extent they admit the harms of fossil fuels, industry representatives sometimes argue the harms are justified by the benefits. But if they believed that--and if they believed consumers and the public would agree--then they wouldn't have spent the last several decades lying about climate science and solutions. The time has long passed to commit to renewable energy sources, which can replace the vast majority of fossil fuel use and are [cleaner](https://substack.com/redirect/f598eda7-299f-45d9-adcf-7683cb6735ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and safer. They're also more affordable--clean energy is now the [cheapest](https://substack.com/redirect/c53d6812-293a-4a61-9582-79d7aed1ed4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) form of electricity, a tipping point that would have arrived much sooner without Big Oil's campaign of deception and suppression that Raymond helped spearhead.
On Raymond's death, ExxonMobil [stated](https://substack.com/redirect/dca394bc-47a7-468d-91d8-282f2fcfc97e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that his "legacy will forever remain a pillar of this company." That is undoubtedly true for his legacy of climate deception, which ExxonMobil and its co-conspirators have continued building on to this day. Of course, they have [updated](https://substack.com/redirect/1deb08f8-8259-49e6-8b24-d27f34c03bb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their talking points. In place of Raymond's explicit climate denial, one recent strategy is to portray their companies and fossil fuel products as contributing to climate solutions when they know otherwise. For example, ExxonMobil spent $175 million [marketing](https://substack.com/redirect/102e2a5b-e25a-4280-a3a6-5e4892c34c60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its development of algae biofuels as the answer to global warming, despite [warnings](https://substack.com/redirect/0d847aa9-d884-404a-a3db-7103f675fe16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the corporation's own scientists that such claims were "completely impossible to achieve." The details have changed, but the basic move--weaponize disinformation to block a clean energy transition--remains the same. Raymond's pillar of deception still stands.
When all is said and done, Raymond and his ilk may bear responsibility for more death and destruction than any of history's worst villains. His co-conspirators are still aggressively working to worsen a climate crisis that may cause hundreds of millions, and possibly even [billions](https://substack.com/redirect/c0cffa4e-68d0-473c-a6e8-aa74d19ea188?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), of avoidable deaths.
Unlike the countless victims of climate deception--the [mother](https://substack.com/redirect/1589b034-0eaa-4fe4-acd2-0ee8c115ee11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) killed by extreme heat that would have been [virtually impossible](https://substack.com/redirect/9593c211-f1fc-4d17-b090-412837bafcf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) but for climate change; the [family](https://substack.com/redirect/69ff3cb5-8b1f-4c03-9418-4acf864f1a7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) swept away by a [climate-exacerbated](https://substack.com/redirect/a41dd57b-5fa8-44d1-8e73-e5f3d9718d56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) hurricane; the [farmers](https://substack.com/redirect/556c8b2d-2468-44a7-89a3-4d218d8b183f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) starving in a drought made [100 times more likely](https://substack.com/redirect/15ee90fa-e7da-47a4-a304-f983ba3f084e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by climate change--Raymond had the privilege of dying of natural causes at the end of a long life. He never faced accountability.
But Raymond was far from the only actor responsible for unleashing climate chaos on our world. His successors are still at large, fueling the same planetary arson he fanned for decades. Raymond may be gone, but his work remains a crime in progress. It must be halted.

name: AOC
subject: We can make a new world.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
We don't have to live like this anymore.
#
I grew up in a working-class family.
My mom cleaned houses and my dad worked to build a small business. My parents worked themselves to the bone so that my brother and I could just have a shot.
And for a moment there, it looked like we were going to make it: we had a home, bills were a little less stressful to pay, and I was doing well in school. What may have looked like a modest life to others was a dream come true for us.
But suddenly, when I was a teenager, my dad was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer. He passed away in September of 2008, just as the economy crashed in the Great Recession and millions of jobs across this country vanished.
It felt like the world of our family fell apart as the larger world was falling apart too.
Overnight, my mom was left to figure out how to provide for two kids by herself, put them through school, keep our house, pay off my dad's medical bills — all on a house cleaner salary.
That's how I became a waitress. Because it was millions of innocent working families who paid the price, while the billionaires and thieves who defrauded our financial system got off richer than ever before. **And not a single one of them went to jail**.
And you know what?
**_That_ is the story that Republicans mock — not just mine, but all of ours — when they say a waitress or working person is unqualified to serve in Congress**.
I tell this story not because it is special, but because of how _common_ it is.
While the details may differ, so many of us know what it feels like for life to be one bad day, one bad piece of news, one major setback from everything feeling like it's going to fall apart.
**We don't have to live like this anymore**.
We can make a new world, a better country, where we can fight for the dignity of all people.
And it looks like **living wages**.
It looks like **stable housing**.
It looks like **guaranteed health care**.
And it looks like **respect for all of our differences** , no matter who we are or where we come from.
That means that we must choose to out-organize the oligarchy. We will and must do away with the power of big money.
And that is why, even as a waitress with a long shot campaign, I decided that **I would never take money from lobbyists or corporations — and I never will**.

Every donation helps us mobilize, organize, and fight for the working class in the places that need it most.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

clean_body: We don't have to live like this anymore. I grew up in a working-class family. My mom cleaned houses and my dad worked to build a small business. My parents worked themselves to the bone so that my brother and I could just have a shot. And for a moment there, it looked like we were going to make it: we had a home, bills were a little less stressful to pay, and I was doing well in school. What may have looked like a modest life to others was a dream come true for us. But suddenly, when I was a teenager, my dad was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer. He passed away in September of 2008, just as the economy crashed in the Great Recession and millions of jobs across this country vanished. It felt like the world of our family fell apart as the larger world was falling apart too. Overnight, my mom was left to figure out how to provide for two kids by herself, put them through school, keep our house, pay off my dad's medical bills — all on a house cleaner salary. That's how I became a waitress. Because it was millions of innocent working families who paid the price, while the billionaires and thieves who defrauded our financial system got off richer than ever before. And not a single one of them went to jail. And you know what? That is the story that Republicans mock — not just mine, but all of ours — when they say a waitress or working person is unqualified to serve in Congress. I tell this story not because it is special, but because of how common it is. While the details may differ, so many of us know what it feels like for life to be one bad day, one bad piece of news, one major setback from everything feeling like it's going to fall apart. This past week, I joined Ben Meiselas on the MeidasTouch podcast to talk about the importance of this Senate race, and how crucial it is to have leaders in Washington that understand the needs of their constituents.
(You can watch my interview here on [YouTube](https://substack.com/redirect/e91fe4d3-b0dc-4c25-bde1-e1634273413f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
Here's how it went.
* * *
**Ben Meiselas:** _I want to talk about the Senate race. How important it is nationally, how important it is in North Carolina. I want to begin, though, by just reflecting on the very concept of leadership. You know, when I think about your tenure as governor of North Carolina, one of the things that I always think about is nobody necessarily said that was that Democratic Governor, that was the guy who owned the Republicans, you know, the way, right now I think this MAGA Republican movement likes to frame things, and how politics is so kind of gamified right now._
_I was just, you know, it 's refreshing for me to see the opening of the Obama Presidential Library, you know, different presidents, different policies, plans, just standing up there._
_Whether I agreed or disagreed, they represented a continuity and a peaceful transition of power and dignified leadership that I just feel is missing. The very concept of leading right now with compassion, empathy, thought, expertise._
_I just wanted to pick your brain on that before we really get into the race._
**Gov. Cooper:**_You know, people want government to work, Ben. A lot of people don 't pay attention to the politics of it. They just want their kids to go to good schools, they want health care, they want a solid retirement, they want a good paying job, they want safe communities. More than ever, we need leaders who are ready to step up and do the job._
_I was a Democratic Governor in North Carolina for eight years. I was limited to two terms. I had a Republican legislature for every single moment that I was Governor, and yeah ... I found ways to use my executive authority to help people._
_We got Medicaid expanded, most Southern states couldn 't do that, but we did it. 725,000 people now have more health insurance. I got a Republican legislature to pass a law to get us to carbon zero in our power sector by 2050._
_We were able to get all 99 of our hospitals to sign up for the largest medical debt relief program in the country. People who have civil judgments against them because they didn 't have health care insurance, and you can't get a credit card, you can't buy a house. Sometimes you can't even qualify for rent. So far, we've wiped away six and a half billion dollars in medical debt for more than two and a half million North Carolinians._
_I had Mary come up to me, and show me the letter. She 'd been writing a check for $80 a month. It was a big deal for her on a fixed income. She showed me how that $54,000 had been wiped away. It changed her life._
_We need more people in politics who want to do something rather than people in politics who want to be something, and that everything they do is calculated toward gaining or maintaining their power. I think people are sick of it. It 's time to get competent, decent people back into government, who respect our Constitution, who believe in checks and balances in our democracy. I believe our best days are ahead of us._
_It 's hard to believe right now with the destruction we've seen, and with the people in charge, like my opponent, Michael Whatley, who was chair of the RNC, and who continues to support these horrible policies like the slush fund that wants to pay out money to these January 6 rioters and insurrectionists who assaulted police officers._
_We don 't need those kinds of leaders, and I appreciate coming on your show, because this is going to be a tight race. We haven't elected a Democrat in North Carolina since 2008. Go to [roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/f594a77c-b205-4174-9f73-059d4e79d698?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to help us out. We've got to flip this seat from red to blue to begin those changes of getting people in government who want to actually do something to help people._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5d6a2f19-1bb5-4e76-8cdc-72020309ac52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Ben Meiselas:** _Your opponent in this race, Michael Whatley, former RNC chair, a real architect of Project 2025, an architect of all of the pain that people are feeling across the country, and very particularly as well in North Carolina. You 've got the Make Stuff Cost Less tour, where you're going around speaking with the people of North Carolina. Talk to us about what people are telling you there, whether it's as it relates to child care, grocery, credit scores. What are people experiencing? Because this isn't a Democrat, Republican, Independent thing -- what your opponent, Michael Whatley, and Donald Trump did while they were talking about triumphal arches and reflecting pools that now are like sludgy green algae riddled, you know, when they're out there, triumphal arches, they're screwing over the people also._
**Gov. Cooper:** _Yeah, Michael Whatley was a big oil and utility company lobbyist for years and pushed tax breaks for his buddy millionaires, and he owns individual stocks and big oil companies and utility companies, and he 's making a personal killing on all of this and has pushed all of these policies._
_But then, I will run into Cynthia in Rocky Mount, who just now is having to decide whether it 's worth paying child care. She needs a second income for her family, but she just may not be able to work anymore because she can't afford the child care._
_Seeing $60 a month extra in utility bills from Stephanie, who 's in Charlotte, who's telling me that she's even turning her thermostat up high into the 70s, higher than it's ever been and then she's still getting $60 a month more in insurance._
_I talked to Jarrod, who 's graduated from college, and he's excited. And then he looks at what he's going to get paid and how much rent he's going to have to pay. The housing costs are through the roof._
_We 've had hundreds of thousands of people lose health care in North Carolina because Michael Whatley encouraged and this administration pushed the One Big Beautiful Bill that took those health care subsidies away, and now they're struggling to get health care. And remember on Medicaid expansion, Republican Thom Tillis, who is there now, stood up on the floor and said, "I can't vote for this One Big Beautiful Bill because I don't know what I'd tell the people of North Carolina." He knew that many people were going to lose their health insurance, and remember, the Medicaid cuts will come after the election. And we know that a lot of people in North Carolina are going to be facing that._
_Too many people now just have too much month at the end of the money. I 've got a plan to make stuff cost less at [roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/f594a77c-b205-4174-9f73-059d4e79d698?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), you can go and review our specific policy proposals, starting with things like taking back the constitutional authority on trade and tariffs, and getting rid of these chaotic tariffs that are sending costs through the roof for consumers and small businesses._
**Ben Meiselas:** _You know, I think another issue, too, that I 'm hearing, and I'd love to get your thoughts about it, is not getting nearly enough attention. It's just how significantly people's credit scores are dropping. I know it's not a topic that people often talk about._
_I just remember when I got out of college and law school, I never had a credit card, and I realized very quickly I couldn 't do anything because I didn't have any credit. And so, you know, and I learned very quickly, you know, wait a minute, you know, I have this law job, but I can't get an apartment, I can't get places, you know, without having credit, and one of the things that I feel like with credit card delinquencies and everything, and that it's a real kind of silent situation that no one really wants to talk about, but it's really holding so many people back, and right now in North Carolina, and across the country, people are getting hit because they're tapping into more and more credit card debt, they're late on their payments, and this thing's just growing and growing and growing and growing in a typical kind of Trump fashion. What he wants to do, dump this on the next guy or gal, and have them kind of deal with it, but this problem is growing right now day by day._
**Gov. Cooper:** _Well, it just shows you that it 's not just anecdotal, people telling you these stories. When you see credit scores going down, you know people are having a hard time affording their bills right now, and not only do we see that empirical data, we also see data from Vanguard and Fidelity for telling us that people are not saving as much, they're having to dip into their saving account, and then they're even having to dip into their retirement account just simply to make ends meet. That tells us we have a massive problem where inflation, the cost of living, is simply outpacing people's paychecks right now, and we have to do something about that, you know._
_First, you need someone who cares about it. I mean, this administration, along with my opponent, Michael Whatley. I 'll tell you that the bad thing for me about Michael Whatley is that he will do and say whatever this President tells him to do and say, and that it's going to bring down hundreds of millions of dollars on my head. We've already seen two Republican groups say that they're gonna place almost $100 million in ads against me in this race. The good thing for me is that Michael Whatley will do and say whatever this President tells him to do and say. Therefore, he is saying things like "prices are down, we've defeated inflation, the economy is great, everything is fine," and we have seen that from this administration that if you can't recognize a problem, then how are you going to fix it?_
_And the people in North Carolina know it 's a problem because they're having to face it every day. A story I heard the other day, and I've heard this more than once. People going to the grocery store, they go every week, they get the same thing for their family, that cash register is just going up and up. And a guy was telling me about a family ahead of them went through, and the total came up, and they said "that can't be right." And the clerk said, "Yeah, I'm afraid it's right." It's painful to watch a family remove things from a grocery basket cart and put it back on the shelf because they can't afford it. That's wrong on multiple levels, and if you don't have leaders in Washington who care about that, then that's a problem. And that's why people need to step up right now, get involved, make sure we take back the Senate and the House. We can't take back the US Senate unless we flip North Carolina. That's why I got into this race. I had not planned to go to Washington, but I knew I had the best chance to win this race. I knew that we have a hard time electing Democrats to U.S. Senate in North Carolina. Time to get it done._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5d6a2f19-1bb5-4e76-8cdc-72020309ac52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Ben Meiselas:**_Before we go. Governor Cooper, anything else you want to say to our 7 million subscribers out there?_
**Gov. Cooper:** _So, I appreciate the work that you do, Ben, shining a light on the chaos in Washington. I know that your listeners and your viewers want to step up right now. You can go to[ roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/f594a77c-b205-4174-9f73-059d4e79d698?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to find out what we're doing, not only help us financially, but also you can sign up to volunteer. There are things you can do remotely for our campaign._
_This is going to be a tight one. Yeah, we 're a little bit ahead in most of the polls right now, some have it a lot closer, but in North Carolina, Democrats often have been ahead, ahead, ahead, until they're not._
_When I first ran for Governor in 2016 against the Republican incumbent, I was pretty far ahead. Ended up winning by about 10,000 votes out of 5 million. We know things break toward Republicans toward the end in North Carolina. We just can 't lose this race. I need your help out there, guys. And thank you, Ben, again for having me on your show._
**Ben Meiselas:** _Governor Roy Cooper, thanks for all you 've done. Thanks for devoting your life to actual public service._
_When I do these interviews, sometimes I wake up in the morning, you know, and you see all these headlines, and I 'm reporting on them in the thick of it, you know, and you just see the behavior, you see the character, the low character of some of these people, and I'm like, what is this? This is not what I grew up with, this is not what I went to law school._
_And then I get to talk to people like you, and I 'm like, all right, you give me hope. So, thank you._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/5d6a2f19-1bb5-4e76-8cdc-72020309ac52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/94dffb43-2f7a-49e4-a790-bc2e5723aba6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
As I told Ben, Washington needs leaders who are ready to step up, get the job done and actually care about the people they're representing. We know that to take back the Senate, we have to win in North Carolina. Our best days are ahead of us, so I hope you'll consider chipping in a few dollars or signing up to knock doors before Election Day.
Thanks for reading. You can watch my full interview [here](https://substack.com/redirect/e91fe4d3-b0dc-4c25-bde1-e1634273413f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

More than ever, we need leaders who are ready to step up and do the job. I was a Democratic Governor in North Carolina for eight years. I was limited to two terms. I had a Republican legislature for every single moment that I was Governor, and yeah ... I found ways to use my executive authority to help people. We got Medicaid expanded, most Southern states couldn 't do that, but we did it. 725,000 people now have more health insurance. I got a Republican legislature to pass a law to get us to carbon zero in our power sector by 2050. We were able to get all 99 of our hospitals to sign up for the largest medical debt relief program in the country. People who have civil judgments against them because they didn 't have health care insurance, and you can't get a credit card, you can't buy a house. Sometimes you can't even qualify for rent. So far, we've wiped away six and a half billion dollars in medical debt for more than two and a half million North Carolinians. I had Mary come up to me, and show me the letter. She 'd been writing a check for $80 a month. It was a big deal for her on a fixed income. She showed me how that $54,000 had been wiped away. It changed her life. We need more people in politics who want to do something rather than people in politics who want to be something, and that everything they do is calculated toward gaining or maintaining their power. I think people are sick of it. It 's time to get competent, decent people back into government, who respect our Constitution, who believe in checks and balances in our democracy. I believe our best days are ahead of us. It 's hard to believe right now with the destruction we've seen, and with the people in charge, like my opponent, Michael Whatley, who was chair of the RNC, and who continues to support these horrible policies like the slush fund that wants to pay out money to these January 6 rioters and insurrectionists who assaulted police officers. We don 't need those kinds of leaders, and I appreciate coming on your show, because this is going to be a tight race. We haven't elected a Democrat in North Carolina since 2008. Go to to help us out. We've got to flip this seat from red to blue to begin those changes of getting people in government who want to actually do something to help people. Ben Meiselas: Your opponent in this race, Michael Whatley, former RNC chair, a real architect of Project 2025, an architect of all of the pain that people are feeling across the country, and very particularly as well in North Carolina. You 've got the Make Stuff Cost Less tour, where you're going around speaking with the people of North Carolina. Talk to us about what people are telling you there, whether it's as it relates to child care, grocery, credit scores. What are people experiencing? Because this isn't a Democrat, Republican, Independent thing -- what your opponent, Michael Whatley, and Donald Trump did while they were talking about triumphal arches and reflecting pools that now are like sludgy green algae riddled, you know, when they're out there, triumphal arches, they're screwing over the people also. Gov. Cooper: Yeah, Michael Whatley was a big oil and utility company lobbyist for years and pushed tax breaks for his buddy millionaires, and he owns individual stocks and big oil companies and utility companies, and he 's making a personal killing on all of this and has pushed all of these policies. But then, I will run into Cynthia in Rocky Mount, who just now is having to decide whether it 's worth paying child care. She needs a second income for her family, but she just may not be able to work anymore because she can't afford the child care. Seeing $60 a month extra in utility bills from Stephanie, who 's in Charlotte, who's telling me that she's even turning her thermostat up high into the 70s, higher than it's ever been and then she's still getting $60 a month more in insurance. I talked to Jarrod, who 's graduated from college, and he's excited. And then he looks at what he's going to get paid and how much rent he's going to have to pay. The housing costs are through the roof. We 've had hundreds of thousands of people lose health care in North Carolina because Michael Whatley encouraged and this administration pushed the One Big Beautiful Bill that took those health care subsidies away, and now they're struggling to get health care. And remember on Medicaid expansion, Republican Thom Tillis, who is there now, stood up on the floor and said, "I can't vote for this One Big Beautiful Bill because I don't know what I'd tell the people of North Carolina." He knew that many people were going to lose their health insurance, and remember, the Medicaid cuts will come after the election. And we know that a lot of people in North Carolina are going to be facing that. Too many people now just have too much month at the end of the money. I 've got a plan to make stuff cost less at , you can go and review our specific policy proposals, starting with things like taking back the constitutional authority on trade and tariffs, and getting rid of these chaotic tariffs that are sending costs through the roof for consumers and small businesses. Ben Meiselas: You know, I think another issue, too, that I 'm hearing, and I'd love to get your thoughts about it, is not getting nearly enough attention. It's just how significantly people's credit scores are dropping. I know it's not a topic that people often talk about. I just remember when I got out of college and law school, I never had a credit card, and I realized very quickly I couldn 't do anything because I didn't have any credit. And so, you know, and I learned very quickly, you know, wait a minute, you know, I have this law job, but I can't get an apartment, I can't get places, you know, without having credit, and one of the things that I feel like with credit card delinquencies and everything, and that it's a real kind of silent situation that no one really wants to talk about, but it's really holding so many people back, and right now in North Carolina, and across the country, people are getting hit because they're tapping into more and more credit card debt, they're late on their payments, and this thing's just growing and growing and growing and growing in a typical kind of Trump fashion. What he wants to do, dump this on the next guy or gal, and have them kind of deal with it, but this problem is growing right now day by day. Gov. Cooper: Well, it just shows you that it 's not just anecdotal, people telling you these stories. When you see credit scores going down, you know people are having a hard time affording their bills right now, and not only do we see that empirical data, we also see data from Vanguard and Fidelity for telling us that people are not saving as much, they're having to dip into their saving account, and then they're even having to dip into their retirement account just simply to make ends meet. That tells us we have a massive problem where inflation, the cost of living, is simply outpacing people's paychecks right now, and we have to do something about that, you know. First, you need someone who cares about it. I mean, this administration, along with my opponent, Michael Whatley. I 'll tell you that the bad thing for me about Michael Whatley is that he will do and say whatever this President tells him to do and say, and that it's going to bring down hundreds of millions of dollars on my head. We've already seen two Republican groups say that they're gonna place almost $100 million in ads against me in this race. The good thing for me is that Michael Whatley will do and say whatever this President tells him to do and say. Therefore, he is saying things like "prices are down, we've defeated inflation, the economy is great, everything is fine," and we have seen that from this administration that if you can't recognize a problem, then how are you going to fix it? And the people in North Carolina know it 's a problem because they're having to face it every day. A story I heard the other day, and I've heard this more than once. People going to the grocery store, they go every week, they get the same thing for their family, that cash register is just going up and up. And a guy was telling me about a family ahead of them went through, and the total came up, and they said "that can't be right." And the clerk said, "Yeah, I'm afraid it's right." It's painful to watch a family remove things from a grocery basket cart and put it back on the shelf because they can't afford it. That's wrong on multiple levels, and if you don't have leaders in Washington who care about that, then that's a problem. And that's why people need to step up right now, get involved, make sure we take back the Senate and the House. We can't take back the US Senate unless we flip North Carolina. That's why I got into this race. I had not planned to go to Washington, but I knew I had the best chance to win this race. I knew that we have a hard time electing Democrats to U.S. Senate in North Carolina. Time to get it done. Ben Meiselas:Before we go. Governor Cooper, anything else you want to say to our 7 million subscribers out there? Gov. Cooper: So, I appreciate the work that you do, Ben, shining a light on the chaos in Washington. I know that your listeners and your viewers want to step up right now. You can go to to find out what we're doing, not only help us financially, but also you can sign up to volunteer. There are things you can do remotely for our campaign. This is going to be a tight one. Yeah, we 're a little bit ahead in most of the polls right now, some have it a lot closer, but in North Carolina, Democrats often have been ahead, ahead, ahead, until they're not. When I first ran for Governor in 2016 against the Republican incumbent, I was pretty far ahead. Ended up winning by about 10,000 votes out of 5 million. We know things break toward Republicans toward the end in North Carolina. We just can 't lose this race. I need your help out there, guys. And thank you, Ben, again for having me on your show. Ben Meiselas: Governor Roy Cooper, thanks for all you 've done. Thanks for devoting your life to actual public service. When I do these interviews, sometimes I wake up in the morning, you know, and you see all these headlines, and I 'm reporting on them in the thick of it, you know, and you just see the behavior, you see the character, the low character of some of these people, and I'm like, what is this? This is not what I grew up with, this is not what I went to law school. And then I get to talk to people like you, and I 'm like, all right, you give me hope. So, thank you. As I told Ben, Washington needs leaders who are ready to step up, get the job done and actually care about the people they're representing. We know that to take back the Senate, we have to win in North Carolina. Our best days are ahead of us, so I hope you'll consider chipping in a few dollars or signing up to knock doors before Election Day. Thanks for reading. You can watch my full interview . | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Roy Cooper PO Box 1190, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

name: James Carville, Senior Democratic Strategist
subject: My honest assessment of New Hampshire:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
The math to flip the Senate runs through New Hampshire. Here’s why that should concern you.
Hi. It's James Carville.
I’ve been watching Senate races for decades. What I’m seeing in New Hampshire right now is keeping me up at night — and it should concern y’all too.
I put together a brief memo. Read it. Then let’s help Chris Pappas win this race.
**[If you don’t need convincing, rush a donation to Chris Pappas’s campaign now.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260622_2.aCgbc9&refcode=em20260622-2&t=10&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)**
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260622_2.aCgbc9&refcode=em20260622-2&t=11&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)**
* * *
**SPRING 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON NH-SEN**
**FROM:** James Carville, Senior Democratic Strategist
**TO:** Interested Parties
I need to be clear with you about where things stand in the race for New Hampshire’s open Senate seat.
**The New Hampshire Senate race has been in the margin of error for months — and it’s not getting the attention it deserves.**
* Three recent polls show this race in a dead heat:
* Emerson (March 2026): Pappas 45–Sununu 44
* St. Anselm (March 2026): Pappas 46–Sununu 43
* St. Anselm (November 2025): Pappas 44–Sununu 41
* All of these polls show this race **within the margin of error. The race has been functionally tied for months.**
* New Hampshire’s open Senate seat is sitting in a dead heat with significantly less financial firepower on our side than we have in other Senate races.
* This race will almost certainly be decided by whether Chris Pappas has the resources to compete on the airwaves and on the ground in the final stretch.

**The GOP knows exactly what’s at stake here — and they’re already moving.**
* The Senate Leadership Fund has committed over $17 million to elect John Sununu — their largest investment in New Hampshire in a decade.
* John Sununu is not a back-bench candidate. He has a famous New Hampshire political name (his father and his brother both served as governor), a history of winning statewide, and the full weight of the Republican donor machine behind him.
* And here’s something voters in New Hampshire deserve to know: Sununu left the Senate in 2009 and spent the years following building a personal fortune — with assets estimated as high as $36 million — through corporate board positions and investments in oil and gas companies, including ExxonMobil, Shell, and more. He left New Hampshire, cashed in, and now wants to come back.
* Republicans understand the math perfectly. They don’t need to flip five seats. They just need to flip New Hampshire’s Senate seat and make Democrats’ path to a majority impossible.

**New Hampshire has decided elections before — and the margins are razor thin.**
* In 2016, the last time New Hampshire had a race for an open Senate seat, the race was decided by just 1,017 votes.
* When Democrats chart a path to retaking the Senate majority, New Hampshire is not optional. If Chris Pappas loses, Democrats need to flip five seats instead of four. That math does not exist.

**There is a recent and painful precedent for underestimating a close race.**
* Bob Casey narrowly led in Pennsylvania polling for virtually the entire 2024 cycle — and lost in an upset that shocked the entire party.
* A race that has been tied for six months is not a comfortable position. It is a warning sign. I have seen what happens when we assume a race is in-hand and the resources don’t follow.
* We cannot afford to let New Hampshire’s 2026 race echo Pennsylvania’s in 2024.

**Chris Pappas has what it takes to win — but the outside spending gap is real.**
* Pappas has won New Hampshire’s toughest congressional district four times. He knows how to reach voters across the aisle. His campaign has outraised Sununu candidate-to-candidate with $4.2 million cash on hand to Sununu’s $1.9 million.
* But that advantage disappears the moment the Senate Leadership Fund’s $17 million hits the airwaves. In a race decided by a handful of votes, being drowned out on TV by Republican money in the final weeks is the ballgame.
* This is the moment to make sure New Hampshire doesn’t become the race you wish you’d paid more attention to.

* * *
Listen. The math is simple: Democrats hold New Hampshire, and there’s a path to a majority. Democrats lose it, and nothing else on the map matters.
Chris Pappas needs resources now — before this race gets away from us.
**[Give what you can right now. Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260622_2.aCgbc9&refcode=em20260622-2&t=12&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260622_2.aCgbc9&amount=5&refcode=em20260622-2&t=13&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)**
Thank you for your support. Let’s elect Chris Pappas and flip the Senate.
– James Carville
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260622_2.aCgbc9&refcode=em20260622-2&t=14&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260622-2&t=15&refcode2=7334_582294_L27TJg&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)**
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with grassroots supporters like you. However, if you would like to change your subscription preferences, here are some options:
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.chrispappas.org/signup/cps_receive_fewer_emails/?t=16&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)
* [Update Your Information](https://act.chrispappas.org/signup/cps_update_your_information/?t=17&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)
* [Unsubscribe](https://act.chrispappas.org/unsubscribe/cps_unsubscribe/?t=18&akid=7334%2E582294%2EL27TJg)

Email us: [teampappas@chrispappas.org](mailto:teampappas@chrispappas.org)

| This sponsored message from Just The Truth is on behalf of Hillsdale College[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/RNz%2BstypXtZDpXdsBerOcNhYRBakpbpDpjGaqY%2Fua9aXA9gfEtdiGHcWcArb%0AHjQbNnG%2B%2BuJIsYoGom%2B%2FYAbAW1y%2FNoYdXFRb0H4Q7rwt2dmiurEM8rdEUCl9%0ADJub5bvowIhSQr2NvvrVJofCK4SmNik41RSd62IAG7hre%2Fes7FxTt2Q0RS%2Bg%0AvR396JgADwvNNCCjofGAtkxojRLiCfQTOQ%3D%3D%0A/98dc96262d7d506a)Dear Friend of Liberty,As we approach America’s 250th anniversary, I have a question for you: **what story will the next generation learn about our country?** You’re an intelligent and civically engaged person. It’s a magnificent course, perfect for in-home viewing or with a small study group.We produced this course to help restore intelligent patriotism, especially in young people, which is essential for the survival of free government.**Will you claim your copy of “The Great American Story” DVD box set to add to your home library? We cannot let that happen, especially as America prepares to mark its 250th anniversary.**You can make a difference.** With your gift today, you will help restore intelligent patriotism in the hearts of millions of Americans, just in time for the 250th celebration!Thank you for helping others learn the truth about our history and America’s great heritage of liberty. body:
| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/sZJt3wEgAJV?e=b3e15466e8&c2id=331453342f3244bc132aedaded0bd94c)
| | | | |
---
| | Hi Peter, it's Claire.Tomorrow, NY-07 votes.This campaign has always been about something bigger than one election. It has been about whether working people still have the power to shape the future of their communities. Whether tenants, immigrants, union members, young people, and families who are tired of being ignored can come together and build something stronger than the money and influence stacked against them.Tomorrow, we get our answer.And before that happens, I want to ask you one last time: [**can you chip in tonight and help us turn out every last voter before the polls close tomorrow?**](https://us.list-manage.com/605riCm9R0o?e=b3e15466e8&c2id=331453342f3244bc132aedaded0bd94c) For more than a year, this campaign has been powered by people who believed that our government should belong to the people who keep this city running. The nurses who work double shifts. The teachers who buy supplies out of their own pockets. The delivery workers biking through the rain. The tenants fighting to stay in the neighborhoods they helped build. The union members who know that solidarity is stronger than any billionaire's checkbook.Those are the people who built this campaign. And those are the people I will fight for in Congress every single day.
---
| [Chip in Tonight](https://us.list-manage.com/BOLXYyVqJvX?e=b3e15466e8&c2id=331453342f3244bc132aedaded0bd94c)
---
| | We knocked on more than 300,000 doors. More than 23,000 people chipped in to power this campaign. Thousands of volunteers gave their time because they believed that working people deserve a government that fights for them. No corporate PAC money. No real estate money. No wealthy interests calling the shots.Just people. Just organizing. Just the belief that if we stand together, we can build a future that works for all of us.Tomorrow, we have the chance to send that message all the way to Washington. But first, we have to get every supporter we can to the polls.[**Please chip in tonight and help us finish this campaign the same way we built it: together.**](https://us.list-manage.com/76s3J2IxgrL?e=b3e15466e8&c2id=331453342f3244bc132aedaded0bd94c) No matter what happens tomorrow, I will always be grateful for what we built together. But I believe we are about to show this country what working people can do when we organize.See you on the other side.In solidarity,
Claire
---

A man inspects buildings destroyed by Israeli airstrikes in Nabatieh, southern Lebanon, June 21, 2026. Photo by Ali Hashisho/Xinhua via Getty Images.
BEIRUT, Lebanon--Fadel Jaber returned to Nabatieh in southern Lebanon on Thursday, anxious to see his home for the first time since he was forcibly displaced by the Israeli military three months ago. The previous day, the U.S. and Iran had signed a memorandum of understanding to end the war between them that included a specific stipulation to halt the fighting in Lebanon. Believing that the city would be safe, Jaber joined thousands of people heading south on roads choked with traffic, the flow of vehicles slowed by damaged bridges targeted by Israeli airstrikes.
After several hours, he finally reached his home, but the respite turned out to be temporary. Around midnight, the earth began to shake from heavy bombardment.
"It was a disaster," Jaber told Drop Site News. "Nonstop warplanes, nonstop bombing. The strikes seemed to come from every direction."
His son in the nearby village of Kfar Joz received a call from the Lebanese Civil Defense telling him that they were evacuating residents and that he should meet them at the emergency vehicle down the street. Minutes after leaving, his building along with three others in the vicinity were flattened by Israeli bombs.
"The strikes weren't concentrated in one area of military importance; they were widespread and targeted civilian areas," said Abbad Romani, a medic and spokesperson with the Islamic Health Authority in Nabatieh. Romani spent the night assisting at Najdi Hospital, where the dead and wounded were brought throughout the brutal Israeli assault. "They were so intense that people weren't even able to leave."
Around 5 a.m, Jaber decided to leave his home once again and try to head back to Beirut. Within an hour of departing, he got word that the building adjacent to his and another across the street were both bombed, and his own home was heavily damaged. The Israeli military later declared it had conducted more than 150 strikes across Lebanon, the majority concentrated in Nabatieh and its surrounding villages. At least 47 people were killed that night, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry, though Romani expected the toll to grow as more bodies were recovered.
"It was the most violent night we witnessed this war. The work was very tough," Hassan Fakih, the head of the Lebanese Civil Defense in Nabatieh, told Drop Site. "Drones targeted anything moving on the roads, which limited our ability to rescue the injured," he said, adding that the waves of airstrikes were supplemented with heavy artillery shelling.
Despite reports emerging on Friday of a ceasefire deal between Israel and Hezbollah, Israeli strikes continued overnight killing scores more people. Hezbollah fought back killing at least six Israeli soldiers and wounding more than 20. But by Saturday afternoon the attacks subsided and a relative calm has held for the first time since March.
## **Bombing the Ceasefire**
Multiple residents told Drop Site that the events on Thursday bore resemblance to April 8, when the Israeli military struck more than 150 locations across Lebanon in the span of ten minutes after the United States and Iran first agreed to a temporary ceasefire--an attack that killed over 350 people and is referred to in Lebanon as "Black Wednesday."
The lack of warning, the breadth and scale of the bombardment, and the timing were echoed in Thursday's assault on Nabatieh. In both cases, Israel launched an intensified attack after Washington and Tehran reached an agreement that included a ceasefire in Lebanon in no uncertain terms.
According to local witnesses, the assault coincided with an Israeli attempt to advance through the village of Kfar Tebnit and seize Ali Taher hill, which overlooks Nabatieh and which Israel claimed serves as a major strategic location for Hezbollah. Residents reported heavy clashes between Hezbollah fighters and Israeli troops, with the Israeli military illuminating the night sky with flares as it evacuated wounded soldiers. At least four Israeli soldiers, including a battalion commander, were killed by Hezbollah anti-tank missile fire on Thursday night, while at least 17 others were wounded.
Since March, when Hezbollah entered the war alongside Iran, Israel has killed more than 4,100 people in Lebanon and displaced over 1.2 million. Hezbollah has continued to retaliate against Israel's military campaign and has stunned Israel with its ability to inflict losses on occupation forces. More than 30 Israeli soldiers have been confirmed killed in action since March 2.
The first provision of the MOU signed last week mentions Lebanon three times, calling for "the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" as well as "ensuring the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon."
In response to Israel's bombardment of Lebanon on Thursday, Iran refused to de-link Lebanon and allow the agreement with the U.S. to move forward, declaring it would close the Strait of Hormuz, jeopardizing a key provision of the MOU. Iran also told mediators it was prepared to suspend the agreement entirely and launch retaliatory strikes against Israel, [a senior Iranian official told Drop Site](https://substack.com/redirect/17e34dfe-7018-447c-86d1-89bb53ae8fc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Nevertheless, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has insisted that Israeli troops would remain in a "security zone" in southern Lebanon, which runs several kilometers along the border into Lebanese territory and encompasses more than 60 Lebanese villages, indefinitely. "Our fighters in southern Lebanon have full freedom of action to thwart any direct or emerging threat against them or against the residents of the north. The IDF has no restrictions in this matter," Netanyahu [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f5aeedf6-8549-4363-8902-aa4aacf13c5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday. "I stand firm on the fact that we will remain in the security zone in southern Lebanon for as long as is required to protect the residents of the north and all the citizens of the state."
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz also said that Israeli troops would not withdraw from Beaufort castle--also known as Qalaat al-Shaqif--in southern Lebanon. "Israel has no intention of withdrawing from the Beaufort, which is an integral part of the security zone in Lebanon and essential for the defense of the Galilee settlements and IDF forces," Katz wrote on X.
Hezbollah Secretary General Naim Qassem rejected Israel's continued occupation of Lebanese territory, saying in a televised address on Sunday Israeli troops "remaining on Lebanese land is impossible. There are no security zones for Israel...we have a national army which deploys, and it is responsible for preserving sovereignty, and it is who we cooperate with." He also condemned the hypocrisy of Israel's position. "A ceasefire means Hezbollah does not fire and Israel is free to occupy anywhere. We do not want such a ceasefire."
Even Lebanese President Joseph Aoun--who at the outbreak of the latest phase of the war on March 2 regularly condemned what he called Iranian interference in Lebanese affairs, declared a ban on Hezbollah military activity, and supported efforts to expel Iran's ambassador from Beirut--appeared to warm to Tehran's stance. Aoun held direct talks with Israeli officials in Washington--the first publicly acknowledged direct negotiations in decades--that were conducted alongside the U.S.-Iran negotiations in what was presented as two separate tracks. Since the signing of the MOU, however, Aoun has welcomed the deal and spoken by phone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
Yet the continued occupation of large swathes of southern Lebanon by the Israeli military risks scuppering the deal, which explicitly calls for the "territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon."
As Israel's bombardment has halted, Lebanese families once again began to slowly return to the south, including to Nabatieh and its surrounding villages, many to find their homes reduced to rubble.
Jaber said that despite relative calm and the progress made in the U.S.-Iran talks over the weekend in Switzerland, he didn't believe the war was over. "It won't end until the Israelis have completely withdrawn from Lebanese land," he said. He planned to return to Nabatieh on Tuesday to begin repairs on his home in preparation to move back for good. He said he could not afford another month of rent in Beirut and did not want to endure life in a government shelter. "Better to die in dignity."

In both cases, Israel launched an intensified attack after Washington and Tehran reached an agreement that included a ceasefire in Lebanon in no uncertain terms. According to local witnesses, the assault coincided with an Israeli attempt to advance through the village of Kfar Tebnit and seize Ali Taher hill, which overlooks Nabatieh and which Israel claimed serves as a major strategic location for Hezbollah. Residents reported heavy clashes between Hezbollah fighters and Israeli troops, with the Israeli military illuminating the night sky with flares as it evacuated wounded soldiers. At least four Israeli soldiers, including a battalion commander, were killed by Hezbollah anti-tank missile fire on Thursday night, while at least 17 others were wounded. Since March, when Hezbollah entered the war alongside Iran, Israel has killed more than 4,100 people in Lebanon and displaced over 1.2 million. Hezbollah has continued to retaliate against Israel's military campaign and has stunned Israel with its ability to inflict losses on occupation forces. More than 30 Israeli soldiers have been confirmed killed in action since March 2. The first provision of the MOU signed last week mentions Lebanon three times, calling for "the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon" as well as "ensuring the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon." In response to Israel's bombardment of Lebanon on Thursday, Iran refused to de-link Lebanon and allow the agreement with the U.S. to move forward, declaring it would close the Strait of Hormuz, jeopardizing a key provision of the MOU. Iran also told mediators it was prepared to suspend the agreement entirely and launch retaliatory strikes against Israel, . Nevertheless, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has insisted that Israeli troops would remain in a "security zone" in southern Lebanon, which runs several kilometers along the border into Lebanese territory and encompasses more than 60 Lebanese villages, indefinitely. "Our fighters in southern Lebanon have full freedom of action to thwart any direct or emerging threat against them or against the residents of the north. The IDF has no restrictions in this matter," Netanyahu on Monday. "I stand firm on the fact that we will remain in the security zone in southern Lebanon for as long as is required to protect the residents of the north and all the citizens of the state." Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz also said that Israeli troops would not withdraw from Beaufort castle--also known as Qalaat al-Shaqif--in southern Lebanon. "Israel has no intention of withdrawing from the Beaufort, which is an integral part of the security zone in Lebanon and essential for the defense of the Galilee settlements and IDF forces," Katz wrote on X. Hezbollah Secretary General Naim Qassem rejected Israel's continued occupation of Lebanese territory, saying in a televised address on Sunday Israeli troops "remaining on Lebanese land is impossible. There are no security zones for Israel...we have a national army which deploys, and it is responsible for preserving sovereignty, and it is who we cooperate with." He also condemned the hypocrisy of Israel's position. "A ceasefire means Hezbollah does not fire and Israel is free to occupy anywhere. We do not want such a ceasefire." Even Lebanese President Joseph Aoun--who at the outbreak of the latest phase of the war on March 2 regularly condemned what he called Iranian interference in Lebanese affairs, declared a ban on Hezbollah military activity, and supported efforts to expel Iran's ambassador from Beirut--appeared to warm to Tehran's stance. Aoun held direct talks with Israeli officials in Washington--the first publicly acknowledged direct negotiations in decades--that were conducted alongside the U.S.-Iran negotiations in what was presented as two separate tracks. Since the signing of the MOU, however, Aoun has welcomed the deal and spoken by phone with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. Yet the continued occupation of large swathes of southern Lebanon by the Israeli military risks scuppering the deal, which explicitly calls for the "territorial integrity and sovereignty of Lebanon." As Israel's bombardment has halted, Lebanese families once again began to slowly return to the south, including to Nabatieh and its surrounding villages, many to find their homes reduced to rubble. Jaber said that despite relative calm and the progress made in the U.S.-Iran talks over the weekend in Switzerland, he didn't believe the war was over. "It won't end until the Israelis have completely withdrawn from Lebanese land," he said. He planned to return to Nabatieh on Tuesday to begin repairs on his home in preparation to move back for good. He said he could not afford another month of rent in Beirut and did not want to endure life in a government shelter. body:
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=335%2E127862%2EtcxwDO)
Folks,
**Lying Lombardo’s most recent attack ad just got exposed.** Let me explain:
Lombardo's PAC started running their latest attack ad a few weeks ago. The ad was so egregious that one local news outlet ran a fact-check and concluded that multiple parts of it were false.
And then — this is the part I can't get over — one of the workers featured in the ad admitted in an interview afterward that he only did it for the money and in fact _voted for me_ in the primary! It’s such a jarring admission that even members of the media have called it “embarrassing” and “an unforced error” on Lombardo’s part.
**Lying Lombardo has spent nearly $7 million on ads over four months, and the polls haven’t moved an inch in his favor. That’s why he’s resorting to fallacies and smears.**
He’s desperate — and he should be. But here’s the thing: **he’s also incredibly well-funded.** If we’re going to win, we need the resources to beat back his lies and get on the airwaves ourselves.
Lombardo is one of the most vulnerable Republican governors up for re-election in the country. Cook Political Report rates this race a toss-up. **We have the momentum to flip Nevada blue.**
**[But we can't afford to sit back and let these smears gain any more traction. Chip in $5 right now, and let's keep the pressure on:](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260622_1_ak.9XlAcz&amount=5&refcode=em20260622-333&t=3&akid=335%2E127862%2EtcxwDO)**

The Knicks win should have been a net positive for New York City. The team amassed huge support nationwide, giving the 2026 NBA Finals their **[highest](https://substack.com/redirect/84016ee1-97eb-4783-b292-e26ab7332c7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** viewership ratings since 1998, with a peak of 20.9 million viewers. Additionally, it was a prime opportunity for the city to see a spike in economic revenue. Estimates believe that the championship series may have generated as much as **[$465 million](https://substack.com/redirect/e52d58ee-47ae-4979-ab69-8a07f5d0df6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for the local economy. Local businesses including bars and restaurants saw their revenue spike as much as **[60%](https://substack.com/redirect/618adff8-0c33-4167-b4ff-ff2ed7e2fafb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on game nights, as both residents and visitors flocked to their favorite eateries.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly90aGVjYXBpdGFsaXN0bWFnLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.qrw88hYzK1fgaLcX2t4udSzlwXrRVWyOMPKIo__ewuM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=203105216)
Unfortunately, it is hard to justify these fiscal achievements when businesses, fans, and the entire city have to fear for their safety. The Knicks win didn't lead to a sustained crime wave, but it showed New Yorkers' willingness to riot, even amidst their city's success. Those conditions are not conducive to a healthy, growing society. The temporary financial boost doesn't offset long term issues, like the **[5,000](https://substack.com/redirect/364eaa98-da0b-4dc5-94ec-2a6f60aa16ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** NYC businesses that closed in 2025.
The result of these crime-fueled outbursts is that both citizens and businesses are leaving the city in droves. In recent years, retail chains such as Target, Walgreens, and CVS have each closed multiple of their New York City locations due to wide scale shoplifting and theft, which had frequently threatened the safety of both their employees and customers. After the assassination of United Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson, several prominent New York companies echoed the sentiment that "**[Business leaders all take very personally what happened to Brian Thompson. "](https://substack.com/redirect/43c703e0-e6fb-45df-a2cb-adaf8ae01340?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** In May, the Wall Street private equity firm Apollo Global Management announced **[plans](https://substack.com/redirect/7d2617eb-74f1-4357-b62a-479ac323fd53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to open a headquarters outside of New York, partially due to employee safety concerns in New York.
Other New Yorkers report concerns about being mugged or robbed during their daily commute. Last year, only **[42%](https://substack.com/redirect/c6a150e8-8e25-4939-88cf-849d1f90f6bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of New York City residents rated their neighborhood safety as 'good', and the share of residents who felt safe walking alone at night dropped from 705 in 2017 to 59% in 2025. There has also been a drop in the percentage of people who feel safe riding the subway, and a **[32.57%](https://substack.com/redirect/dd753d9d-4a72-46ec-86bf-f75297ca5452?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** rise in total violent felonies on NYC transit systems.
New Yorkers are becoming afraid of the city they love. The uptick in vandalism, rioting, and violence over what should have been a celebration is proof that their fears are justified.

Election experts at Sabato’s Crystal Ball just moved Alaska’s U.S. Senate race from Lean Republican to Toss-Up. = This is a big deal — and it confirms what we already knew: Mary Peltola can win this race. Friend — Warren Petersen, the Republican candidate for Arizona Attorney General, just told more than 18,000 Arizona Dreamers — people who grew up here, went to school here, work here as nurses, firefighters, and small business owners — to "be ready to be deported or prosecuted." Not criminals. Not strangers. Our neighbors. Petersen didn't stop there. He's now earned the endorsement of Joe Arpaio — the former sheriff held in criminal contempt of court for racially motivated policing. Together, they're promising to bring back the politics of fear that once made Arizona a national symbol of anti-immigrant extremism. Arizona voters lived through SB1070. We remember what happened when politicians used government power to terrorize immigrant families. Communities were torn apart. Families lived in fear. And Arizona became a cautionary tale for the rest of the country. Peter, Pete Hegseth just personally blocked nine qualified Navy officers from promotions that a board of senior admirals had already approved. Three of them are women. Two are Black men. The final list he released did not include a single woman in a Navy that is 21% female. He did the same thing to the Army earlier this year and to the Air Force, the same Air Force I proudly served in for two decades. **Let me tell you about my first day in command of 150 Airmen, because the sexism and racism Hegseth is dragging back into the military is exactly what I spent my career fighting to push out of it.**
---

Fellow American - Let me tell you something they don't teach you in Washington.

**I grew up in the back of a bar.**
Not a fancy restaurant. Not a supper club. A beer joint, pool hall, and liquor store on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - the Sanitary Cafe. My parents ran it. We lived behind it. I swept the floors, wiped down the tables, and fell asleep listening to the sounds of working people winding down after a long shift at the textile mill.

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=f20578b977fb4f618e67a6891dead66a&_e=40OwMrdCBlOflKZhI8yBoOo7gojJlDFplGufnihrKzm2VDsUrotIWwTvfdMt25MtW9dd-DBkWJO3XeQGlsqp6oKGZhpz6vu8sLTX6XZikh7ydy1RJfFwrcFYMw0VwsNeYb8eZUynvn8p0eFx7l5eR0OWh7T2KseT63G1CwOwDhPK9m8vWVih5K3ucNENN9Bs3DtqjYiXTYkVyLXX6zaceJIgABDJzFAXV8CDEY4Ljj6ixxlrSQo33niDCZXDTigHJ6xl_twpoBKxwAQNFby1Ja6iP0TRAOHO75rIDsVj_Da0wmk9f0S6kt4-UX_8VCsEMo9Am2IALK0dpd6fuJoNhLLUP-EvvlQMJPl3TxWLws91GavIEGm2Njyei79j0sVyM8-wJcblLlypWt_fpNM6AXrsHtfmhHuUlAIGeZdiDsGWYlqWKZQgdFlBL8zKs11bkkMsnGNHPhTc8UgtK-Z3TDWy1YJkaLfA97LYjIscREz_TdkrYj23Onvu3Rpto5uHc2vgfkCyu2sendC_28Tuwem6439IfzD2Yq3k0jzrWcWZ5XwiiVx0rloknKUojK12pk7D1jEOC4bFxWXV0fdGpXPVkPNA0XF51aUzRBROrmTL_CZmRu-jnXXfUnQtEAwBsiClQYvRto0ITLqvMqjlNKG_cYVc4kCLIrHmhjVqOsgyKC0Vm0Xyk6e9JEVPPeOqn2HcSiUcAIETlle8Pr9_r9NFjo6ATmrJLr7mT8zIBcNwDRDaj47lqfAIhdMlrYLnEKsrVwpm441QasfilOopJxx2iVp9lbprJTdd1nSP_jO9JYowmppmR81pfkMYIaMX)
Neither of my parents finished high school. But they worked as if the sun were always going down, and they believed - truly believed - that their kids would go further than they did.

I was the first in my family to go to college. And while I was there, I lost them both. Mom and Dad, died within two years of each other. I came home on weekends to keep the business going and helped raise my little sister, Darline, who was just 13.

I didn't have a safety net. I had no choice but to climb.

Even after South Carolinians sent me to the Senate, I kept serving in the Reserves. I've been to Afghanistan. I've been to Iraq. I've stood next to kids from small towns just like Central who signed up because they believe in something bigger than themselves.

That's why I fight so hard, because I know exactly what's at stake.

The people coming to our family's pool hall after a long week - they weren't asking for much. Safe streets. A fair shot. A chance to build something. Those are the same things Americans want today.
