It was built, on purpose, by people with names and addresses -- and it was defended, for nearly eighty years, by money, fear, and a lie so effective it's still doing its job. If it was built, it can be unbuilt. So let's go back to where it started. | | ---|---|--- 1945 After the Second World War, the United States stood at a real crossroads. Soldiers were coming home. The GI Bill had just shown, in real time, what it looked like when veterans got medical care as a matter of course instead of a matter of paperwork. Across the Atlantic, Britain was building the National Health Service out of the rubble of the Blitz. And seven months into a presidency he'd inherited rather than won, Harry Truman stood before Congress and proposed something radically simple: that no American should have to go bankrupt to see a doctor. His plan was single-payer, funded the way we fund Social Security -- through payroll contributions -- so that every American, rich or poor, rural or urban, could walk into a hospital without doing the math first. Truman didn't frame this as charity. He framed it as infrastructure. " Healthy citizens," he told Congress, "constitute our greatest national resource." A healthy population wasn't a private luxury to him -- it was the foundation of a strong economy and a secure democracy. And here's the part that feels like a gut punch: the country agreed with him. When Gallup polled Americans on Truman's plan in November 1945, 59% approved. Only one in four opposed it. A nation exhausted by war, wary of new federal programs in general, still wanted this one. Imagine that -- before the fear campaigns, before "socialized medicine" became a household curse word, before illness became a business model and bankruptcy from it became just a normal feature of American life. The country was ready. The AMA Declares War Then the American Medical Association declared war. The AMA didn't treat Truman's proposal as a policy disagreement to be argued on the merits. It treated it as an existential threat -- to its income, its autonomy, its control over the profession. And in the chill of the early Cold War, it found the perfect weapon: fear , dressed up as patriotism. The AMA branded the plan "socialized medicine" -- a phrase built less to describe than to attack -- and accused the people drafting it of being "followers of the Moscow party line," when the threat of "communism" was the biggest, scariest monster in the American psyche. One widely circulated AMA pamphlet went so far as to attribute a quote to Lenin himself, falsely claiming he'd once called socialized medicine "the keystone to the arch of the socialist state." It wasn 't true. It didn 't need to be. The goal was never accuracy. The goal was to make ordinary Americans afraid of the very thing that would have protected them. When Truman pulled off his stunning 1948 reelection -- and brought new, younger, courageous Representatives to Congress with him -- the AMA didn't retreat. It escalated. That December, the AMA's House of Delegates voted to assess every one of its 140,000 members an extra $25, real money at the time, to fund what they called resistance to "the enslavement of the medical profession." With that war chest, they hired Whitaker & Baxter, the nation's first professional political consulting firm, to run a campaign that ran into the millions of dollars -- at the time, one of the most expensive lobbying efforts in American history. Their strategy was blunt: give the program an ugly name, and give the fight a villain. The AMA called Truman's plan un-American. Truman turned the word back on them: "is it un-American," he asked, "to visit the sick, aid the afflicted, or comfort the dying?" It was a fair question in 1948. It still is. It Worked. We're Still Paying for It. The AMA's lobbying worked. By October 1950, support for national health insurance had collapsed from 59% to 24%. The bill died -- not because it was unpopular on its merits, but because it had been made to look monstrous. And the playbook the AMA built in those four years became the playbook for every healthcare fight that followed. The same language was recycled against Medicare in the 1960s, against universal coverage proposals through the decades since, against the Affordable Care Act in 2010. Even Dwight Eisenhower campaigned against "socialized medicine" in 1952, borrowing words built specifically to kill a plan that most Americans wanted and had nothing to do with him. And we are still living inside the wreckage. We pay for this every time someone delays treatment because the deductible is too steep to clear. We pay for it every time a mother stays in a job that frightens or exploits her because her child's medication is tied to that insurance card. We pay for it every time a small business loses a good employee to a corporation that can absorb healthcare costs it cannot. We pay for it every time a veteran has to fight, paperwork in hand, for care they already earned in uniform. We pay for it every time someone who did everything right -- worked hard, paid their premiums, followed every rule -- still ends up in medical debt because they had the misfortune of getting sick or injured in the richest country on earth. What the Constitution Actually Promises This is not freedom. A person is not free if they can't leave a job because leaving means losing the insulin, the chemotherapy, the mental health care, or the coverage their child depends on. A family is not free if a single emergency can wipe out their savings, their credit, their housing, in one stroke. A country is not free if getting sick is a financial trap for its own people. Healthcare is not a luxury good, and it is not a reward for being useful to an employer or profitable to an insurer. It is care for the body -- and the body is where freedom actually lives. You cannot exercise liberty from a hospital bed you cannot afford. You cannot pursue happiness while rationing your own medication. You cannot fully participate in a democracy while you're on hold with an insurance company for days, weeks, or months, fighting for a treatment your own doctor already told you that you need. This is where healthcare stops being a policy preference and becomes a constitutional obligation. The Constitution opens with a promise, not a slogan: to establish justice, insure domestic tranquility, provide for the common defense, promote the general welfare, and secure the blessings of liberty. The general welfare isn't an abstraction you wave at from a podium. It's whether a child sees a doctor before a fever turns into an emergency. It's whether an elder ages with dignity instead of fear. It's whether a disabled person gets to live a full life rather than a managed one. It's whether a mother survives childbirth -- without going bankrupt -- in the wealthiest country in human history. It's whether a worker can change jobs, start a business, or care for a sick parent without that decision costing them their coverage. For nearly eighty years, a powerful industry has told us that guaranteeing those things is impossible, unaffordable, un-American. I'd put it the other way. What's un-American is a system where corporations profit from denying care. What's un-American is making people beg for treatment through a phone tree, then get denied by an AI without even the bare consideration of five minutes of human attention. What's un-American is letting medical debt destroy a family while executives and shareholders extract parasitic wealth from human vulnerability. None of this is a personal failure. It is not because families budgeted badly, or workers lacked discipline, or small business owners didn't plan well enough. This is the entirely predictable result of a political system that let healthcare profiteers write the rules eighty years ago -- and has been protecting their handiwork ever since. That's why this history matters. Not as trivia: as diagnosis. And a correct diagnosis is the first thing you need before you can actually heal anything. Military Healthcare: Where It's Already Happening I know this system from more than one angle. My husband was a paramedic, emergency medical technician, and first responder as well as an Army medic trainer, and my father spent his career in Navy medicine, so for our family this has never been an abstraction -- I've watched American healthcare from inside the exam room as well as from the patient's side of the billing desk. My father was a Navy doc, and for as long as I can remember, since I was a small child, he told me the same thing in one form or another: that he could not imagine what it would do to a person to have to check whether their patient could pay before deciding how to treat them. He never had to make that calculation. In the military health system, you treat the sailor, the soldier, the spouse, the kid with the broken arm, in front of you -- full stop -- and the accounting happens somewhere else, later, without anyone going bankrupt over it. That system isn't hypothetical. It's real, it's running right now, and it covers more than nine million active-duty service members, retirees, and their families. Which means the same country that tells the rest of us universal healthcare is too complicated, too expensive, too radical to guarantee has quietly been running a working, no-means-tested version of it for our military families for decades. We don''t have to invent anything. We already know how to do this. We've simply decided, as a matter of policy, that some Americans get that peace of mind and the rest of us have to fight an insurance company for it. That isn't a technical problem. It's a moral one -- and it is, frankly, a matter of national shame. Here's An Example for How This Can Work Here's the part nobody tells you: we already know how to do this. Right now, today, there is a fully designed, fully costed plan sitting in the Washington State Legislature that would cover every single person in this state -- every resident, regardless of immigration status, age, income, employment, or pre-existing condition -- with comprehensive coverage: medical, mental health, dental, vision, reproductive care, the whole picture, free at the point of service. No premiums. No deductibles. No copays. No surprise bills. It's called the Washington Health Trust (SB 5335 in the Senate, HB 1445 in the House), and the organization that has spent years building the case for it, testifying for it, and refusing to let legislators look away from it is . Independent economic analysis estimates the Trust would save the state somewhere between $5 and $13 billion every single year, by cutting out the duplicate(/triplicate, or even quadriplicate) billing departments, the competing insurance bureaucracies, the claim-denial algorithms, and the layer of pure profit-extraction that our current system pays for instead of paying for care. Sit with that for a second. We are not choosing between covering everyone and saving money. We are currently paying more -- much, much more -- to bankrupt hundreds of thousands of our neighbors, to needlessly contribute to tens of thousands of preventable deaths a year, and to burn millions of collective hours of people's lives on hold with insurance companies, all so an unnecessary, baroque, and frankly parasitic layer of middlemen can extract a profit from our sickness. For God's sake. We can do better than this. We are choosing not to. Here's a fact for the moment: this summer, Seattle is hosting matches in the FIFA World Cup -- the biggest sporting event on Earth, 48 nations, the whole world watching. It's become one of those facts that fans keep tallying up nation by nation as they watch: of those 48 countries, t he United States is the only one that doesn 't guarantee its people universal healthcare. We're hosting the party, and we're the only one where a player injured in the game has to pay through the nose to see a doctor afterwards. I am a proud endorser of . I've supported this work for years, long before I was a candidate for anything, because I believe it is simply the right thing to do for the people of this state. And I have personally taken the -- a commitment to refuse contributions over $200 from the executives, lobbyists, and PACs of the corporate healthcare industry that has spent eighty years and counting making sure people like us stay afraid of the very reforms that would help us. I won't take their money. I will take their fight. Care. Courage. The Constitution. I am running for Congress because people in this district are tired of being told to wait while their lives get harder and the powerful get away with more. I am running because "liberty and justice for all" does not come with an asterisk. I am running because a government that exists to secure our rights also has to protect the actual conditions that let people live, work, parent, age, and participate as free human beings -- and that means guaranteeing healthcare, not rationing it. That means ending medical debt. That means standing up to insurance companies and pharmaceutical profiteers instead of taking their checks. That means fully funding the care our veterans already earned. That means protecting reproductive freedom and bodily autonomy. That means treating care work -- for children, for elders, for the disabled, for the sick -- as infrastructure, not as charity we hope someone else provides. I don't take corporate PAC money. I don't take money from foreign interests or defense contractors. I've taken the Patients Over Profits pledge for the same reason Truman fought the AMA and lost: the moment you let an industry write the checks, you've already lost the argument before it starts. I'd rather lose a fundraising email than lose my ability to tell you the truth. We already know how to guarantee healthcare without bankrupting anyone -- we've been quietly doing it for military families for decades. The only reason we haven't done it for everyone else is that a small number of billionaires, and the industries that bankroll their favorite politicians, profit from keeping the rest of us confused, afraid, and fighting each other instead of fighting them. That isn't an accident or a mystery. It's billionaire capture of our political system, plain and simple, and it has to end. The fight ahead is hard, because the money on the other side is enormous -- the same money, more or less, that's been winning this argument since 1949. The moral question underneath it has never changed. Do we believe human beings have dignity, or not? Do we believe freedom belongs to everyone, or only to the healthy and the wealthy? Do we believe government exists to secure our rights, or to protect the business model of the industries that profit from our pain? I know my answer. Care. Courage. The Constitution. A healthcare system that serves the people. A government that finally answers to them. A country where "liberty and justice for all" means exactly what it says -- to every single one of us, no asterisks. Peter,

Stephen Miller and Sean Hannity had a lot to say about Abdul on Fox News.

[ A ]A screenshot from Sean Hannity's Fox News show. The chyron says
'El-Sayed Continues To Call For ICE To Be Abolished'

He called us “violent extremists,” just because Abdul said what
Michiganders already know: We need to abolish ICE.

Not reform it. Not retrain it. Abolish it.

Donald Trump has turned ICE loose on our communities. Agents in masks.
Neighbors disappeared. Children behind bars. Families torn apart.

It is happening in Michigan right now, including at private GEO Group
detention centers like the one in Baldwin.

Abdul has said we need to abolish ICE since 2018. He is the only candidate
in this race who has. Because you cannot reform an agency that acts like
it is above the law. ICE is out of control. It cannot be fixed. And
Michiganders know it.

This election is going to be defined by that question. Who will actually
stand up to Trump's ICE? Not who says the right thing in a super PAC ad.
Who has the record and the spine to do it... and that candidate is Abdul.

So, Fox News is scared. They are not attacking a long-shot progressive
campaign. They are attacking one with real momentum. They are trying to
scare voters into believing that their common sense is dangerous.

But here is what should worry us even more than Stephen Miller and Sean
Hannity.

AIPAC is spending tens of millions of dollars on ads across Michigan to
boost our primary opponent, Haley Stevens. And the entire message of those
ads is that Haley Stevens is the candidate who will hold ICE accountable.

That is a lie. Haley Stevens voted to thank ICE officers. When she visited
the detention facility in Baldwin, she praised ICE for having “women in
positions of leadership.” She is hardly the “hold ICE accountable”
candidate she claims to be.

But it doesn't matter how big the lie is when you have tens of millions of
dollars to repeat it over and over. And it's working. A new poll just
showed Haley Stevens closing the gap on Abdul's lead.

This is exactly how they win. They outspend us. They distort the truth.
They drown out the one candidate who is actually telling Michiganders the
truth about ICE.

We cannot let them.

This campaign will never have AIPAC's money. We will never have a super
PAC spending tens of millions to lie on our behalf. All we have is you.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260622-2-ak._Z9T8g&amount=10&refcode=em20260622-2419&t=1004&akid=2421%2E251025%2EQsfV4E ]So we are asking you directly. Will you chip in right now to help Abdul
fight back and get the truth out before it is too late?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260622-2-ak._Z9T8g&amount=10&refcode=em20260622-2419&t=1023&akid=2421%2E251025%2EQsfV4E ]Donate $10 ››

Every dollar goes straight to putting Abdul's message in front of Michigan
voters. That ICE is out of control. That it must be abolished. That Abdul
is the only candidate in this race who has said so, and meant it, for
years.

Stephen Miller and Sean Hannity can call us whatever they want. Fox News
can run whatever scare campaign it wants. AIPAC can spend whatever it
wants.

We are not backing down.

Thank you for being in this fight,

Team Abdul

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260622-2-ak._Z9T8g&amount=10&refcode=em20260622-2419&t=1024&akid=2421%2E251025%2EQsfV4E ]Donate ››

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240911%2E444211%2Ejzq-O3)
The law that governs how most Americans register to vote was written in 1993, and it was built around the DMV: Register to vote when you get your driver’s license.
_Simple, right? Not anymore._
Here’s the reality today: Gen Z isn't getting driver's licenses. Only 26% of 16-year-olds have a license today. By 18, that number is still just 60%. Between rising costs, driving anxiety, and better public transit in major cities,an entire generation is coming of age without ever setting foot inside a DMV.
Because Texas completely blocks online voter registration, Powered by People is doing the hard work to reach these young voters exactly where they are.
We go directly to them — on college campuses, at concerts — to help them get registered, and personally stay in touch with them until and after they vote.
**Democrats have lost winnable races in Texas by razor-thin margins that still haunt us. But it doesn’t have to be that way.**
We know that our organizing moves the needle.
In 2024, the voters our volunteers personally stayed in touch with turned out at 79%. (To put that in perspective, 18-29 year olds not in our program turned out at a rate of 39%.)

Whatever happens next, I’m coming to you tonight with gratitude. We have built this campaign over more than a year with thousands of grassroots donations, and I am so honored to know that this team has my back. **Together, we will win tomorrow – and then take the fight directly to Mike Lawler.** I’m running for Congress not because this was ever part of some big life plan. But because the country I was willing to die for, the one I’ve lost countless friends defending, is becoming something I barely recognize. We cannot let this happen. Not on our watch. I used to tell my soldiers that doing the right thing when it’s easy, when it comes with no personal cost, that’s just doing your job. But doing the right thing when it comes with real sacrifice, to your career or even your life, that is courage. For 250 years, our country has endured some of its darkest chapters because ordinary people chose to live with courage. They knew that America and our democracy was worth fighting for. _That is exactly what this moment demands of us now._ We have never been a perfect union. But we have always been in the pursuit of forming a more perfect one. And that comes with work, sacrifice, and love. Right now, this chapter in American history, how it ends is not yet written. Independent polling shows that I am the only Democrat running in NY-17 that beats Mike Lawler. There are no paths to take back the House without winning this district. There is no margin for error. So, one last time, can I count on you to chip in and help fuel our get out the vote effort tomorrow? I promise every dollar makes a difference. We have built this campaign over more than a year with thousands of grassroots donations, and I am so honored to know that this team has my back. Together, we will win tomorrow – and then take the fight directly to Mike Lawler. I’m running for Congress not because this was ever part of some big life plan. But because the country I was willing to die for, the one I’ve lost countless friends defending, is becoming something I barely recognize. We cannot let this happen. Not on our watch. I used to tell my soldiers that doing the right thing when it’s easy, when it comes with no personal cost, that’s just doing your job. But doing the right thing when it comes with real sacrifice, to your career or even your life, that is courage. For 250 years, our country has endured some of its darkest chapters because ordinary people chose to live with courage. They knew that America and our democracy was worth fighting for. That is exactly what this moment demands of us now. We have never been a perfect union. But we have always been in the pursuit of forming a more perfect one. And that comes with work, sacrifice, and love. Right now, this chapter in American history, how it ends is not yet written. Independent polling shows that I am the only Democrat running in NY-17 that beats Mike Lawler. There are no paths to take back the House without winning this district. There is no margin for error. So, one last time, can I count on you to chip in and help fuel our get out the vote effort tomorrow? I promise every dollar makes a difference. Defending democracy is the biggest team sport out there. Tomorrow, let’s get the jerseys on, take the field, and win this thing. subject: Pulling back the curtain
body:
Ahead of my biggest FEC deadline yet next week, I want to pull back the curtain and explain a few things.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6532?source=&t=1&akid=1852%2E124072%2Ej3NSTz)
| | | |
---
Peter,
[**At the end of this message, I’m going to ask if you will chip in $5 to my campaign for U.S. Senate ahead of our major FEC fundraising deadline coming up in eight days**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk660&amount=5&t=8&akid=1852%2E124072%2Ej3NSTz) – but first, I want to pull back the curtain and explain why it’s so important that you do.
The end of this month marks the most important fundraising deadline yet in this Senate race and one of the most critical tests of the grassroots movement we’ve built here in North Carolina.
After the 11:59 p.m. deadline next Tuesday, candidates like me are legally required to report our fundraising numbers from the last three months to the Federal Election Commission. Shortly thereafter, those numbers will be made public for all to see.
Since experts say that North Carolina is the best chance for Democrats to flip a seat, and that Senate control hinges on this race, I’m the GOP’s top target for defeat. They’ve already committed to spend nearly $100 million so far just on attacking me.
So as soon as our report goes live, everyone – from my MAGA opponent to national Republicans and their far-right billionaire allies – will be looking closely. **Very closely.**
If they detect any signs of weakness, you can bet they’ll flood the airwaves with millions more to drown us out. That’s a risk we can't afford at this point in the race.
We have to show everyone that our grassroots movement is thriving and unstoppable – that we have what it takes to build the strongest voter outreach and mobilization program our state has ever seen. That’s just what it’s going to take to win what’s expected to be the most competitive and expensive Senate race in U.S. history.
So I'm personally asking: [**Will you chip in to my campaign before our critical FEC deadline next week? Every donation sends a powerful message that folks like you have my back in the fight to flip North Carolina blue.**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk660&amount=5&t=9&akid=1852%2E124072%2Ej3NSTz)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

One race. One loss. If the Left takes control, they will shut Trump down immediately — blocking his agenda, burying his priorities, and ensuring nothing meaningful gets done. That’s why I wrote a confidential note meant only for a small number of conservatives who still understand what’s at stake. This was not written for the public, and it won’t stay available for long. **You were one of the people I felt I had to share it with, Peter.** Please don’t put this off. I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong.

_**Faith. Family. Freedom.**_

The Left is doing _everything_ they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored.

**This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.**

Will you stand with me?

Peter, NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani is fulfilling his campaign promises one by one. Last week, he accomplished a big one: 2-K applications officially opened.
That means — for the first time — thousands of New Yorkers will be able to apply for free childcare for their 2-year-olds. It’s a game-changer for so many families.
There’s a lesson here for Democrats: **We need to deliver on our promises.**
This kind of governing is exactly what the people demanded when they elected Zohran. And it’s what people across the country are desperate for. They are sick and tired of politicians who sell out to the highest bidder. They want leaders who will actually work for them. And those are the kinds of candidates we support.
The reason Mayor Mamdani has been able to do this is not because he’s some kind of political genius, it’s because he had the right values and the resources to back him up. It was possible because of you. With your support, we were able to spend $300,000 as his largest backer in the primary.
**Leaders We Deserve is backing dozens of candidates across the country in critical races. We have the opportunity to elect more leaders like Zohran who will actually make progress — not just talk about it. We don’t take a dime of corporate PAC money, so we need grassroots support from folks like you.**

David Hogg
